title: Nothing kills the vibe in Baltimore quite like an injury to Lamar Jackson. This year is no different
summary: Lamar Jackson was a full participant in practice for the Baltimore Ravens, which suggests his latest injury saga could be over sooner rather than later
story: Lamar Jackson was a full participant in practice for the Baltimore Ravens, which suggests his latest injury saga could be over sooner rather than later
OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- Lamar Jackson was a full participant in practice for the Baltimore Ravens, which suggests his latest injury saga could be over sooner rather than later.
Maybe.
“I think the more you’re able to do and respond from and feel from certainly raises your optimism,” coach Jesse Minter said Wednesday. “But again, we’ll kind of see how it goes throughout the week.”
The Ravens play at Buffalo on Sunday.

Since his first full season as a starter in 2019, Jackson ranks seventh in starts among NFL quarterbacks. He's been less durable than fellow MVPs Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes, but other top quarterbacks like Joe Burrow and Brock Purdy have had similar injury issues to the Baltimore star. Yet it's Jackson whose absences are so angst-inducing and opaque.

A combination of factors are at play — the league's culture of secrecy when it comes to injuries, a player whose mindset is hard to read, and a team that comes into every season with high expectations, but has yet to reach a Super Bowl with Jackson.

Coaches often talk about not wanting to give up too much information on injuries because it could help an opponent. That might sound paranoid, but preparing for Jackson is a significant undertaking, and it makes sense that Baltimore would want the other team to think he might play even when it's unlikely.

On the first Wednesday after Jackson injured his ankle this season, Minter said: “There's a lot of time between now and Sunday. ... There will be a point later in the week where we will figure out kind of where it is at.”
That comment — on Oct. 7 — left open at least some possibility of a quick return for Jackson. He's missed three games since then.

The previous coaching staff wasn't much different. When Jackson injured his knee against Denver in 2022, John Harbaugh was quick to declare it was not a season-ending issue. Jackson didn't play again.

The way the Ravens talk about Jackson's injuries creates a cycle in which fans can get their hopes up each week, then are let down when he doesn't play. That makes him appear slow to return, and occasionally Jackson has weighed in himself, pointing out the severity of his injuries. Over a month after his 2022 injury — with a playoff game approaching — Jackson said on social media he'd suffered a grade 2 PCL sprain and his knee was still unstable.
Last week, Jackson spoke with reporters and said he was told he had a high ankle sprain — by no means a routine ailment.
“I’m just trying to move how I move,” Jackson said. “If I can’t do that, I can’t help my team.”
Even after two MVPs, Jackson takes heat for his sporadic attendance at voluntary offseason practices. That may be part of the reason he doesn't necessarily get the benefit of the doubt when hurt.

Then there are his contract negotiations, which rarely seem simple. He played out his whole rookie deal before the team put the franchise tag on him after the 2022 season. A collusion case — with Jackson's situation a big part of it — went to arbitration. The Ravens and Jackson were amicable in public after reaching a deal, but it's always been hard to tell how much contract talks affect him. That's led to wild speculation about his motivation when he misses games while hurt.
The Ravens, Minter included, make a point of talking about how hard Jackson works to get back on the field, but the team often sounds like it too is in the dark about whether or not he'll play.

“I don’t know if it’s because of lack of agent or what, that no one can kind of defend him,” cornerback Marlon Humphrey said. “I do know this: If Lamar Jackson can play, if he’s healthy enough to play, he will play, and that’s kind of all I can say on that.”
Last season, Jackson hurt a hamstring in Week 4. The Ravens lost their next two games without him and were 1-5. After a bye week, he still missed one more game before coming back.

But if Baltimore fans want him to play through more injuries, the rest of that season should have given them pause. Jackson dealt with more issues down the stretch and was not remotely the player he usually is, particularly when it came to his running ability.
“I feel like that was dumb a little bit,” he said last week. “I was still — I’m hurt and I’m trying to help my team win, but I’m not to my full capabilities, not even close to it.”
This season is still young. Jackson could return and play great down the stretch. If not, get ready for more drama.
According to overthecap.com, Jackson carries a cap hit of about $84 million in 2027, the last year of his contract. There will be immense pressure to work out an extension and spread that money out.

But if this season is derailed by Jackson's injury — just like 2021, 2022 and 2025 — and negotiations are difficult, what are the Ravens to do? He turns 30 in January. By his own admission, he's not helping his team as much if he doesn't have mobility.

In between all those health issues, Jackson was the MVP in 2023 and an All-Pro in 2024. He was showing that ability again early this season. That player could be back soon, and all parties better hope so. More than just the 2026 season could be at stake.

title: Man City and Liverpool win penalty shootouts to advance in English League Cup
summary: Manchester City and Liverpool have avoided the fate that befell Arsenal by winning penalty shootouts to advance to the quarterfinals of the English League Cup
story: Manchester City and Liverpool have avoided the fate that befell Arsenal by winning penalty shootouts to advance to the quarterfinals of the English League Cup
Manchester City and Liverpool avoided the fate that befell Arsenal by winning penalty shootouts on Wednesday to advance to the quarterfinals of the English League Cup.
City stayed on course to retain the title by twice coming from behind to draw 2-2 with Brighton at home, then triumph 4-3 in the shootout.

Backup goalkeeper Gerónimo Rulli saved Brighton's last two spot kicks — from Yasin Ayari and Lewis Dunk — to rescue City, which had fallen behind in the shootout when Mateo Kovacic had the team's fourth penalty saved.
In a match that finished a half-hour later, Liverpool beat Chelsea 6-5 in a shootout after a 1-1 draw that saw both goals also come from the penalty spot.
Wesley Fofana missed what proved to be the final kick of the shootout, smashing it well over the crossbar and into The Kop at Anfield as Liverpool fans roared in delight.
Arsenal wasn't so lucky in a shootout on Tuesday, losing in stunning fashion to fourth-tier minnow Fleetwood Town in one of the biggest shocks in the competition's 66-year history.
In other all-Premier League last-16 matchups on Wednesday, Bournemouth beat Aston Villa 3-0, Crystal Palace won 1-0 at Fulham, and Sunderland overcame Brentford 3-2.
Third-tier Bradford City — the beaten finalist in 2013 — joined Fleetwood in advancing to the quarterfinals on Tuesday.
The draw for the last eight is later Wednesday.
On Thursday, Everton hosts Newcastle to wrap up the last 16.

title: Timberwolves say Anthony Edwards will be 'good as new' with no long-term concern after knee surgery
summary: The Minnesota Timberwolves believe Anthony Edwards will be “good as new” following arthroscopic surgery for a lingering injury to his right knee
story: The Minnesota Timberwolves believe Anthony Edwards will be “good as new” following arthroscopic surgery for a lingering injury to his right knee

MINNEAPOLIS -- The Minnesota Timberwolves believe Anthony Edwards will be “good as new” following arthroscopic surgery for a lingering injury to his right knee, president of basketball operations Tim Connelly said Wednesday.

Edwards was scheduled for the cleanup procedure Thursday, after which the Timberwolves will have a clearer timetable for his return later this season, whether that becomes a matter of weeks or months.

Connelly didn't specify the diagnosis, but Edwards was bothered by right knee pain last spring and limited to a career-low 61 games last season. He then suffered a hyperextension of his left knee in the first round of the playoffs that caused a deep bone bruise and kept him out for two games.

Edwards was seen grabbing his knee with a grimace at one point Sunday during the home opener. Even after being listed as questionable to play Monday, Edwards scored 47 points in an overtime loss at Cleveland. His 133 points through four games is a franchise record.

An MRI Tuesday revealed new damage for Edwards that was not detected in previous scans, which were done before training camp and during the playoffs. His condition this summer was not such that a procedure would have been recommended then, Connelly said.

“He wants to play tonight. He looked pretty good the other night, having the 47,” Connelly said before the Timberwolves hosted Golden State. “We’re just concerned about his long-term health. We want to make sure we’re putting him in the best position he can be so he can be the best version he’s going to be for a long time.”
Edwards, ever the intense competitor, consented to the surgery “kicking and screaming,” Connelly said.
“He’s bummed, but Anthony is such a naturally positive and upbeat guy,” Connelly said. “He’s hit all his teammates quickly and said, ‘You guys got it,’ and we’ll roll from there.”

The Timberwolves are already without guard Donte DiVincenzo, who started all 82 games last season before tearing his right Achilles tendon in the same playoff game against Denver during which Edwards hyperextended his left knee. The acquisition of point guard LaMelo Ball remade the lineup and gave the Timberwolves a fresh spark, moving Edwards back to his natural shooting guard spot.

There's plenty of backcourt depth with Ayo Dosunmu and Terrence Shannon Jr. coming off the bench so far this season, with one of them likely to start in the absence of Edwards. Another backup, Bones Hyland, will likely have an elevated role as well.

“We know he brings dynamic scoring, leadership. Tough to fill in his shoes, just from what he does on the floor for us. Nobody can be like Ant, but we've got players who can step in and just take over a game as well,” Hyland said. “Just play team basketball.”
AP Sports Writer Dave Campbell contributed to this report.

title: Despite much-criticized early tipoff, Dream say WNBA Finals Game 6 against Valkyries is a sellout
summary: The Atlanta Dream say Thursday’s WNBA Finals Game 6 against the Golden State Valkyries is a sellout despite its much-criticized 12:30 p.m. Eastern tipoff
story: The Atlanta Dream say Thursday’s WNBA Finals Game 6 against the Golden State Valkyries is a sellout despite its much-criticized 12:30 p.m. Eastern tipoff
ATLANTA -- Game 6 of the WNBA Finals between Atlanta and Golden State on Thursday is a sellout despite its much-criticized 12:30 p.m. EDT tipoff, the Dream announced Wednesday.
The Valkyries lead the series 3-2 and can clinch their first WNBA title with a win in the matinee at State Farm Arena. The Dream need a win to force a Game 7 on Saturday night in California.

There were concerns the early tipoff would have the teams playing the potentially decisive Finals game in a half-empty arena because of fans having work and school obligations. Instead, the sellout means another Atlanta turnout of approximately 17,000 is expected for the third time in the series.

“I think it’s good,” Dream coach Karl Smesko said Wednesday. "I’m glad we’re at State Farm and they got everything worked out. Everybody understands it’s going to be an early start time. Hopefully the crowd gets there early and is ready to support us to a win.”

The Dream played most of their regular-season home games at Gateway Center Arena, which has a capacity of about 3,500. On Oct. 6, the team announced it will play all its home games at State Farm Arena beginning next season after landing a multiyear agreement with the venue.

For the Finals, however, the Dream and WNBA have had to negotiate scheduling conflicts because of a concert and NBA Hawks home games at State Farm Arena. Because the Hawks had a home game against Cleveland scheduled for Thursday night, the decision was made to schedule the early tipoff instead of holding a primetime game at the much smaller Gateway Center Arena.

The decision generated criticism of the Dream, the Hawks and the WNBA. The Dream ownership group of Robyn and Larry Gottesdiener, Suzanne Abair and Renee Montgomery responded with an open letter to fans on Tuesday. The letter said the league was slow to respond to concerns about scheduling conflicts that were raised two months ago.

“As we moved through the playoffs, we reiterated those concerns,” the owners wrote. “Our concerns did not receive the attention, nor the urgency that they deserved. Perhaps it was assumed that the Dream would not make it this far. Perhaps, our place in the Finals was not accounted for. Whatever the reason, the reality is that we are here. We earned our place in the Finals, and our city deserves the opportunity to show up for its team.”

The decision to keep the game at State Farm Arena means a second court transformation of the Finals. The Hawks moved back the start of their game against the Cavaliers from 7 p.m. to 8 p.m. so there will be sufficient time to remove the Dream's court and install the Hawks' court.
The Dream also had an early tipoff for Game 4 at State Farm Arena before the Hawks' night game against Houston.
The Valkyries vowed to address defensive breakdowns following a 97-71 loss to the Dream in Game 3 that left Atlanta with a 2-1 series lead.

Coach Natalie Nakase, center Kiah Stokes and the Valkyries found a fix, holding Angel Reese and the Dream to their lowest-scoring games of the series in a 67-62 win in Game 4 and a 64-55 win in Game 5.
After opening the Finals with three consecutive double-doubles, Reese has made only two field goals in each of the last two games.

“Just trying to match her minutes," Stokes said Wednesday when asked what changed after Game 3. "I think I’ve done the best job on her compared to all of our bigs in the games, so that was just a personal thing. But I think just the increased pressure, especially around the perimeter, because she’s a great passer. So if we can try to limit her assists, too, it’s good for us.”
The Dream ranked third in the league in scoring with 90.8 points per game. The Valkyries allowed a league-low 75.1 points per game.
Reese said she remains confident in the offense.

“It’s just knowing who we are,” she said. "We watched a lot of film, and the mistakes that we made have really just been us. Kudos to Golden State for their defense for sure, but we’ve gotten a lot of great looks. We just haven’t hit the shot yet. It’s coming. I don’t believe it’s not coming.

“We put the work in every single day, Karl has us the most prepared team, so that’s why we have no doubt. I have no doubt this team will come back and fight back and win this Game 6, and then we’ll go on from there.”

title: Rays ace Drew Rasmussen to start World Series Game 5 on short rest against Milwaukee
summary: Drew Rasmussen will start for Tampa Bay on three days’ rest in Game 5 of the World Series against the Milwaukee Brewers on Wednesday night, trying to stave off elimination for the Rays
story: Drew Rasmussen will start for Tampa Bay on three days’ rest in Game 5 of the World Series against the Milwaukee Brewers on Wednesday night, trying to stave off elimination for the Rays

ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. -- Drew Rasmussen will start for Tampa Bay on three days' rest in Game 5 of the World Series against the Milwaukee Brewers on Wednesday night, trying to stave off elimination for the Rays.
A 31-year-old right-hander, Rasmussen threw 89 pitches over 3 2/3 innings in Game 2 on Saturday, getting no decision as Milwaukee rallied for a 5-4 victory and a 2-0 Series lead.

Rasmussen has had three major elbow operations in his career, including Tommy John surgeries in 2016 and 2017 and an internal brace procedure in 2023. The two-time All-Star was 16-5 with a 2.67 ERA in the regular season.
Jacob Misiorowski was to start on regular four days' rest for the Brewers, who have a 3-1 lead in the best-of-seven series after wasting a 12th-inning lead in a 4-3 loss Tuesday.
Tampa Bay used seven pitchers Tuesday: starter Griffin Jax along with relievers Kevin Kelly, Game 1 starter Nick Martinez, Bryan Baker, Tyler Wells, Cam Booser and Ian Seymour.

title: Fleetwood's Cod Army still reveling after pulling off major cup upset over Arsenal
summary: Fleetwood Town and its fans woke up Wednesday still pinching themselves following one of the biggest upsets in English League Cup history
story: Fleetwood Town and its fans woke up Wednesday still pinching themselves following one of the biggest upsets in English League Cup history
Fleetwood Town posed the question: “The biggest cup shock of all time?”
That's what the fourth-tier team asked on social media after knocking Premier League champion Arsenal out of the English League Cup on Tuesday in a penalty shootout.
There was little question about it as Fleetwood fans woke up Wednesday still pinching themselves following one of the biggest upsets in the Cup’s 66-year history.
More than 80 places separate the two teams in the English soccer pyramid. Arsenal’s stellar squad is worth an approximate $1.6 billion, while Fleetwood’s is valued at a relatively paltry $3 million.
Mikel Arteta has steered Arsenal to five trophies, including last season's Premier League title — as well as the Champions League final.
Fleetwood boss Matt Lawlor is less than a year into his first senior managerial position, having been given the job on an interim basis in January before his appointment was made permanent in March.
“I was trying to not cry and I didn’t,” said the 38-year-old Lawlor, who hails from nearby Poulton-le-Fylde. “I’ve managed to hold it. My family, my little boy here, we’re all local.

“I was turning around and people were screaming at me in the crowd and people that I knew and grew up with. Obviously that’s really special and really emotional — to do something that special early in my career as well.”
Here’s some more things to know about the latest giant-killers in English soccer:
Fleetwood is a coastal town in the northwest of England, with a population of around 26,000.
It is more famous for being the place where the lozenge Fisherman’s Friend is manufactured than its soccer team.
The team is nicknamed the Fishermen, while its supporters are called the Cod Army, because of the town’s fishing industry history.
Almost literally. Fleetwood play at Highbury Stadium, which was the scene of Tuesday’s cup upset.
That is the same name as Arsenal’s storied former stadium from 1913-2006 but the link is pure coincidence and the ground is a world away from what the Premier League team is used to.

Fleetwood’s intimate stadium takes its name from a nearby road and has a capacity of just 5,300. It also has only four parking spaces, which meant Arsenal representatives had to find alternatives on the street, according to British newspaper The Guardian.
The match against Arsenal was Fleetwood’s first sell-out in more than a decade.
Fleetwood is most famous for being the team where former England and Leicester striker Jamie Vardy made his name.
Vardy was there for just one season and helped Fleetwood gain promotion out of the fifth tier, and into the English Football League, before getting a move to Leicester in 2012.

The sale of Jamie Vardy to the then Championship side for 1 million pounds ($1.3 million) was for a long time the highest fee ever paid for a player in Non-League, before it was broken two months ago.
Andy Pilley was the chairman and owner of Fleetwood until he stepped down in 2023, shortly before being handed a 13-year prison sentence for fraud. He lost an appeal in February this year.
Pilley invested more than 10 million pounds ($13 million) into the club, which saw the complete renovation of Highbury Stadium during his tenure.
Pilley was convicted in May 2023 for his part in a multi-million pound fraud which duped firms into expensive energy contracts.
His son, Jamie Pilley, took over Fleetwood in May 2024.

Andy Pilley's stewardship sparked a remarkable rise: six promotions in 10 seasons, including entry into the Football League for the first time in 2012 and culminating in a place in the third-tier League One in 2014.
Fleetwood's highest-ever finish in the soccer pyramid was fourth place in League One during the 2016–17 season. The team was relegated back to the fourth tier in 2024.
After Tuesday's nights heroics — Arsenal rested some first-team stars but still picked a strong lineup — Fleetwood will have to immediately turn its attention to Saturday's visit of Bristol Rovers.
Fleetwood is 18th in the 24-team League Two, hovering just above the drop zone after winning just one of its past eight league matches.

“Football’s getting a little bit more, I don’t know, clinical and removed,” Lawlor said. “And that to me, there was that feeling that we all get as football fans. That was what you kind of live for, isn’t it?
“I want us to carry the momentum forward. I want that feeling that we’ve created here to be something that we can recreate on a regular basis.”

title: FIFA politics around Infantino re-election push Japanese official to resign
summary: Two-time World Cup coach Takeshi Okada has resigned as Japanese soccer federation vice president in protest at the politics around FIFA during Gianni Infantino’s campaign to be re-elected
story: Two-time World Cup coach Takeshi Okada has resigned as Japanese soccer federation vice president in protest at the politics around FIFA during Gianni Infantino’s campaign to be re-elected
GENEVA -- Two-time World Cup coach Takeshi Okada resigned as Japanese soccer federation vice president in protest at the politics around FIFA during Gianni Infantino’s campaign to be re-elected.

Japan’s soccer body on Wednesday published Okada’s resignation statement dated last Saturday — 24 hours after the Asian Football Confederation had performed a U-turn by publicly supporting Infantino, who seeks a fourth and final presidential term at an election in March.

Infantino has faced a backlash since July over his failed World Cup sell-off plan and broader management style including ties to U.S. President Donald Trump, provoking a furor from soccer leaders in Europe, North America and — initially — in Asia.
The 70-year-old Okada, who coached Japan at the World Cups of 1998 and 2010, wrote of his belief “that sports should embody integrity.”

“However, the series of actions surrounding this year’s FIFA World Cup represent a significant divergence from my personal convictions,” Okada said in the statement. “As a sportsman, I cannot accept this.”
Okada acknowledged the complexity of Japan’s place in the politics of world soccer's ruling body FIFA and Asia, adding he understood “there are practical reasons for aligning with the AFC’s stance.”

Japan wants to host the men's World Cup before 2050, its federation president Tsuneyasu Miyamoto said at an October 2023 online meeting of the AFC that endorsed Saudi Arabia’s bid to host the 2034 edition.

AFC president Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa had in August joined his fellow FIFA vice presidents, Aleksander Ceferin from UEFA and CONCACAF’s Victor Montagliani, by criticizing Infantino for “deception” and a “fundamental breach of trust” for pushing to sell a permanent stake in World Cup profits to private investors led by Joshua Kushner, younger brother of Jared Kushner, who is married to Trump’s daughter Ivanka.
However, Infantino never lost support from 2022 World Cup host Qatar and seemed to regain trust since August from 2034 host Saudi Arabia.

The two Gulf states are major power brokers in Asian soccer and, last Friday, Bahraini royal family member Sheikh Salman surprised many global soccer observers by announcing the AFC would now endorse Infantino.
The AFC has 46 of the 211 FIFA member federations who will vote in the March 18 election scheduled in Rabat, Morocco.
The 211 members effectively own FIFA as a Switzerland-based non-profit organization, and have been promised $25 million each by Infantino in development funds over the next four years.
European soccer's ruling body UEFA has committed to finding a candidate against Infantino by a FIFA deadline of Nov. 18 to enter the contest.

title: Spanish soccer federation postpones 24 Copa del Rey games after train crash, clubs show solidarity
summary: The national soccer federation says all 24 Copa del Rey games scheduled for Wednesday have been postponed because of the train accident that killed more than 60 people in central Spain
story: The national soccer federation says all 24 Copa del Rey games scheduled for Wednesday have been postponed because of the train accident that killed more than 60 people in central Spain
MADRID -- The national soccer federation has postponed all 24 Copa del Rey games scheduled for Wednesday because of the train accident that killed more than 60 people in central Spain.

Clubs across the country sent messages of solidarity and support to the victims of the accident, which also left dozens injured after a high-speed train slammed into the rear of another one that had stopped on the tracks.
“Shocked by the tragic railway accident,” the federation said.
It said it ordered the postponement of the games “in solidarity with the victims."

“The entire Spanish soccer community stands united in grief over this tragedy and has made itself available to the authorities to assist the victims of this devastating accident,” the federation added.

“Real Madrid C.F. wishes to express its deepest sorrow over the tragic railway accident,” the club said in a statement. “The club extends its condolences to the families and loved ones of those who lost their lives, as well as its affection and solidarity to the injured and all those affected by this terrible accident.”
Barcelona also expressed “its deepest condolences to the victims.”
“The club wishes to convey its support and solidarity to the families and friends of the victims and to wish all those injured a speedy recovery,” it said in a statement.
Atletico Madrid said it joined “in the grief for the victims of the terrible railway accident that occurred this morning.”
Atletico, Barcelona and Real Madrid are among the teams who do not enter the tournament until the round of 32.
The federation said it would later provide a revised tournament schedule. Five top-flight clubs were set to play in the first round on Wednesday: Real Betis, Celta Vigo, Valencia, Alaves and Levante.
First-round games on Thursday have not been postponed. Games were played on Tuesday as well.
The Spanish league has not announced any postponements of this weekend’s games.

title: French protests push UEFA to switch date of Europa League game in Rennes
summary: The prospect of a general strike in France next week amid national protests on cost of living issues has pushed UEFA to change a Europa League match date in Rennes
story: The prospect of a general strike in France next week amid national protests on cost of living issues has pushed UEFA to change a Europa League match date in Rennes
NYON, Switzerland -- The prospect of a general strike in France next week amid national protests on cost of living issues has pushed UEFA to change a Europa League match date in Rennes.
UEFA said Rennes will now host Olympiakos of Greece on Wednesday of next week at 4:30 p.m. local time (1530 GMT) instead of the Europa League’s scheduled program Thursday.
French trade unions are calling for a Nov. 5 general strike during widespread protests that began with students raising concerns about school conditions.
UEFA said it was informed by French public authorities that routine security around the game in Rennes could not be assured on Nov. 5.
The earlier kickoff time next Wednesday avoids a clash with 6:45 p.m. Central European Time (1745 GMT) starts in two Champions League games: Fenerbahce vs. Liverpool and AEK Athens vs. Real Madrid.
The French league also has moved games scheduled this Saturday when police and public authorities are dealing with planned marches and protests.

title: Kimi Antonelli is set to end Italy's 73-year wait for an F1 champion. Here's why it's been so long
summary: Kimi Antonelli is on the verge of becoming Formula 1’s youngest-ever champion, and the first Italian to win the title since Alberto Ascari in 1953
story: Kimi Antonelli is on the verge of becoming Formula 1’s youngest-ever champion, and the first Italian to win the title since Alberto Ascari in 1953
Kimi Antonelli is on the verge of becoming Formula 1's youngest-ever champion, and the first Italian to win the title since Alberto Ascari in 1953.
For a country full of passionate racing fans, the 73-year wait for an Italian champ is puzzling.
Over decades without a title contender to cheer, Italy's legions of passionate “tifosi” fans have worn red to support Ferrari as a team, rather than individual Italian drivers.
Now the 20-year-old Antonelli, reportedly rejected by Ferrari as a child before joining Mercedes, is changing Italy's racing story.
Ahead of Antonelli almost certainly securing the title Sunday in Mexico City, here why it's taken so long for an Italian to win again.
Italy was the center of the racing world when the World Drivers’ Championship began in 1950.
Just five years after the end of World War II, the fledgling Ferrari brand was one of a clutch of teams in Italian racing red fighting for wins.

Italian Nino Farina won the first title for Alfa Romeo, and Ascari added two more for Ferrari in 1952 and 1953. The decade was dominated by Juan Manuel Fangio, F1’s first superstar driver and an Argentine of Italian heritage, who won five championships in his 40s, a feat never seen since.
Financial issues forced Alfa Romeo, Lancia and Maserati out of F1, leaving Ferrari as the sole Italian constructor by 1960 with fewer opportunities for Italian drivers.

Small British teams, mocked by founder Enzo Ferrari as “garagistas” for being run out of backyards and garages, revolutionized F1 with light and nimble designs with the engine behind the driver. By the late '60s, they were dominant.
There have been other teams based out of Italy — including Racing Bulls today — but Ferrari has remained the country's only genuine title contender.
Until the late 1970s it was rare for a season to pass without at least one Formula 1 driver being killed after crashing in races or tests.
Deaths of Italian auto racing stars — including Ascari, killed testing a Ferrari sportscar in 1955 — caused a backlash in Italy.
The influential Vatican newspaper L'Osservatore Romano issued a blistering condemnation of auto racing after the 1958 death of Italy's Luigi Musso, who was driving for Ferrari.
The newspaper likened auto racing to the ancient Roman god Saturn who “continues to devour his own children,” with Musso as one of the victims of a quest to make money regardless of the human cost.

“It is a matter of morality if we consider that, beyond any pretext of science and progress, there is an immediate, concrete industrial and economic interest in such appalling undertakings — an interest that turns the stopwatch into a means of advertising, even if it is linked to the statistics of the victims,” the newspaper wrote.
When a fiery crash left Ferrari's latest Italian star Lorenzo Bandini with fatal burns in 1967, it was a turning point.
“Enzo Ferrari swore after the death of Bandini that he’d never again hire an Italian driver,” American driver Mario Andretti told a conference in Italy last year.

In the 59 years since, only one Italian has driven a full F1 season for Ferrari. Michele Alboreto raced five years for the team in the mid-1980s, finishing second in the 1985 standings. That was shortly before Enzo Ferrari died aged 90 in 1988.

At the same time, the team let other title contenders pass it by, like six-time race winner Riccardo Patrese. That made it harder for Italians to make the step up to F1, faced with the choice of an uncompetitive local team or taking the risk of moving to Britain at a young age.
The most recent Italian to drive for Ferrari in F1 was Giancarlo Fisichella in 2009, standing in for the injured Felipe Massa, but he spent almost all of his career with teams based in England.

Born to an Italian family in what is now Croatia, Andretti won the title with Lotus in 1978 and drove for Ferrari before that. As an Italian American, hiring him was a loophole in Enzo Ferrari's self-imposed restrictions, Andretti has said.

Three-time champion Ayrton Senna of Brazil, widely considered a contender for F1's greatest-ever talent, had Sicilian heritage. Emerson Fittipaldi, a two-time champ in the 1970s, was another Italian Brazilian.

In the 1990s, France's Jean Alesi — born Giovanni in an Italian family — was a race winner for Ferrari. More recently, Massa from Brazil and the Australians Daniel Ricciardo and Oscar Piastri have been F1 title contenders with Italian heritage.
Nicole Winfield in Rome contributed to this report.

title: Turnaround by the Vikings and collapse by the Chargers make for a first in the NFL
summary: The Minnesota Vikings and Los Angeles Chargers are the surprising last teams standing with a zero in either the win or loss column
story: The Minnesota Vikings and Los Angeles Chargers are the surprising last teams standing with a zero in either the win or loss column
The Minnesota Vikings and Los Angeles Chargers are the surprising last teams standing with a zero in either the win or the loss column.

The Vikings beat Indianapolis 16-10 on Sunday and are now the only undefeated team remaining after losses by San Francisco and Kansas City, while the Chargers are the last winless team after Miami beat the New York Jets.

That makes this season the first in the Super Bowl era, according to Sportradar, when the last undefeated team missed the playoffs the previous season and the last winless team made the previous postseason.

While the Vikings and Chargers are on opposite sides of the standings, they are tied in one statistic that shows just how unlikely this 6-0 start is for Minnesota. The teams are averaging 1.5 offensive touchdowns per game for the second-lowest mark in the NFL.

The Vikings scored five TDs on offense in the opener against Green Bay and have only four in five games since then but still keep winning. Minnesota has scored 125 points overall to tie for the second fewest for any 6-0 team in the last 90 seasons.

The Rams scored 116 in the first six games in 1978 on the way to a 12-4 record and a trip to the NFC title game. The Vikings also scored 125 points in the first six games in 1973 in a season that ended with a Super Bowl loss to Miami.

The fast start should bode well for Minnesota as the final undefeated team has made the playoffs every season since 2017. The last team to miss out were the Vikings in 2016 when they were the only undefeated team at 5-0 after six weeks before finishing 8-8 and falling short of the postseason.
Three teams overcame double-digit deficits to win in Week 7, with one of the teams that blew the lead not a surprise.

Cleveland fell behind 14-0 early before beating Tennessee 27-24, Atlanta rallied from 14-3 down to beat San Francisco 29-20 and Cincinnati overcame a 13-0 halftime deficit to beat Baltimore 35-13. That gives the league 20 double-digit comebacks this season to tie for the third most through seven weeks in a nonstrike season.

The Bengals' comeback was particularly noteworthy as it marked the 10th time in the last five seasons that the Ravens lost a game after leading by at least 10 points in the second half. No other team has done it more than six times in that span.

But it's extremely rare for a team to fall behind by that much at halftime and win such a lopsided game. In fact, Cincinnati became the third team in NFL history to win a game by least 20 points after trailing by 13 or more at the half.

It last happened on Nov. 19, 1950, when the Giants came back from 20-7 down at the half to beat the first version of the Baltimore Colts 55-20. Those Colts folded after the season and a new version that now plays in Indianapolis started three years later. Only one other team has done it in NFL history with the Bears coming from 14-0 down at the half to beat the Eagles 49-14 on Nov. 30, 1941.

The Falcons built a 26-14 lead in the fourth quarter after their first-half deficit and that proved too much for San Francisco to overcome. The 49ers are 0-49 in 10 seasons under Kyle Shanahan, playoffs included, when trailing by at least eight points in the fourth quarter. Every other team has at least one win in that scenario in that span, led by the eight for Green Bay and Pittsburgh.

The comeback by Cleveland prevented Tennessee from winning back-to-back games for the first time since 2022. The Titans have gone 65 straight games without consecutive wins to tie the Browns for the longest streak ever at 65, according to Sportradar. Tennessee will set the record next week with a 66th game.
Tampa Bay did go 74 straight without winning consecutive games in a season in the 1980s but did win the final game in 1988 and the opener in 1989 to break up that streak.
The kicking revolution that took over the NFL last season after a change in the kicking ball has abated early this season with the most misses at this point in a season in five years.
There have been 98 missed field goals and extra points so far for the most in the first seven weeks since there were 102 in 2021.

The problem was especially costly for Green Bay last week. Trey Smack missed a 26-yarder in the first quarter and had a 35-yarder blocked in a tie game in the fourth quarter, contributing to the Packers' 20-17 loss to Detroit.

Smack became the first kicker to miss two field goals from 35 yards or closer in the same game since Mike Nugent did it for New England in a 27-13 win against Cleveland in 2019. It was the first time it happened in a loss of three points of fewer since Shaun Suisham did it for Pittsburgh in a 21-18 loss to the Raiders in 2013.
There has been only one other miss in 172 attempts this season from 37 yards or closer and that came in Week 2 when Chicago's Cairo Santos had a 23-yarder blocked in a 9-3 loss to Minnesota.

The Packers aren't the only team with kicking issues this season. The Rams released Harrison Mevis after he missed two field goals in a Week 5 overtime loss to Buffalo, Eddy Pineiro became the first 49ers kicker in 40 years to miss a kick in at least five straight games and Harrison Butker missed two field goals for Kansas City on Sunday night to give him an NFL-worst 15 missed kicks since the start of last season.
Seattle's Dark Side defense proved to be too much against Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs.

The Seahawks beat the Chiefs 20-3 on Sunday night in a win that was more dominating than even the score indicated. Kansas City failed to make it into the red zone even once in the game for the first time in 153 starts for Mahomes in the regular season and playoffs.

The Chiefs went scoreless in the first half for the fifth time with Mahomes at quarterback, tied their fewest points ever in a Mahomes start with a 27-3 loss to Tennessee in 2021 and finished with their second-fewest yards (213) and fewest first downs (11) in those 153 games.

In fact, the Chiefs only had one touchdown the previous week against the Chargers on a run by Kenneth Walker III, marking the first time a Kansas City quarterback started back-to-back without throwing or running for a TD since Alex Smith did it in 2013.

title: Rays stun Brewers with rally in 12th inning and force World Series Game 5
summary: Jonny DeLuca and pinch-hitter Ben Williamson singled home runs in a stunning 12th-inning rally, and the Tampa Bay Rays staved off World Series elimination with a 4-3 win over the Milwaukee Brewers that forced Game 5
story: Jonny DeLuca and pinch-hitter Ben Williamson singled home runs in a stunning 12th-inning rally, and the Tampa Bay Rays staved off World Series elimination with a 4-3 win over the Milwaukee Brewers that forced Game 5

ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. -- Milwaukee was three outs from its first World Series title when Junior Caminero started the bottom of the 12th inning with a grounder to third. Thousands of Brewers fans who trekked to Tropicana Field to witness the long-awaited moment started to cheer.
Not so fast.
Third baseman Joey Ortiz bounced the throw, and the ball glanced off first baseman Jake Bauers’ mitt for an error.
One of the most stunning rallies in World Series history started to unfold.

Liam Hicks, Jonny DeLuca, Chandler Simpson and pinch-hitter Ben Williamson followed with consecutive singles in a 15-pitch span against rookie Shane Drohan, and the Tampa Bay Rays staved off elimination Tuesday night with a 4-3 win that forced Game 5.

“Sometimes the game tests you. Sometimes the game makes you want to dig deep,” Brewers captain Christian Yelich said. “It’s all part of the journey, all part of the experience, and that’s part of our story.”

Milwaukee rookie Cooper Pratt hit a tiebreaking home run off Ian Seymour in the top of the 12th for a 3-2 lead, sending the Brewers sprinting out of the dugout in excitement as they sensed completing the first Series sweep since 2012.
Milwaukee's bullpen, led by seven outs from Aaron Ashby, had combined for seven straight scoreless innings, before Caminero reached against Antonio Senzatela.
Ortiz grimaced.
“I've got to make that play," he said. “Just no excuse about it.”

Caminero appeared to hurt his left foot but stayed in the game. Brewers manager Pat Murphy brought in Drohan, a 27-year-old left-hander who had not pitched since a one-inning start in Game 4 of the National League Championship Series on Oct. 15.
With Pratt shifted toward second for the left-handed batter, Hicks hit an opposite-field grounder through the vacated shortstop hole and into left field as Caminero slid headfirst into third.
“For just regular D, that's right at Coop,” Drohan said of the defensive alignment.

Pinch-runner Cedric Mullins replaced Caminero before DeLuca, who had made sparkling catches to deny Yelich in the third and William Contreras in the fourth, hit a grounder past the mound as Drohan tried in vain to make a behind-the-back snag. The ball bounced into center as Mullins tied the score at 3.
Nick Fortes ran at second for the slower Hicks. After missing a bunt attempt and pulling back another while taking a called strike, Simpson lined a single into center, loading the bases.
Sal Frelick moved in from left to form a five-man infield, with three defenders on the left side and everyone playing in.
Williamson, who had been 1 for 15 in the postseason, batted for Victor Mesa Jr.
"It’s what you dream of as a player to be in that spot,” Williamson said.

On the game's 367th pitch, he hit a chopper that kicked up chalk from the foul line 7 feet from home plate. The ball bounded high over Bauers and onto the grass in short right field. Fortes sprinted across the plate with the winning run, then headed toward first to join his jumping teammates in foul territory.
“That was totally what I told him to do,” Rays manager Kevin Cash said, drawing laughs.
Drohan walked off, his head bowed.
“Definitely hard. I’m human," he said softly. “I knew what I was walking into. I just didn’t do the job there.”

Tampa Bay became the fourth team in World Series history to avoid elimination with an extra-inning comeback, according to OptaSTATS, joining the 1912 Boston Red Sox, 1986 New York Mets and 2011 St. Louis Cardinals — who all went on to win titles.
“We've got a lot of fight in us. We’re never going to shy away," Simpson said. “We were going to keep fighting until the end — the last inning, the last out, the last play, the last pitch."

Game 5 in the best-of-seven matchup is Wednesday night at Tropicana Field, with NL Cy Young Award favorite Jacob Misiorowski scheduled to start for the Brewers. Cash said he hadn't decided on a starter yet.
Tampa Bay became just the fifth of 26 teams that fell behind 3-0 in the World Series to win Game 4. The previous four lost Game 5.
Of 43 teams to trail 3-0 in any best-of-seven postseason matchup, the only one that rebounded to win was the Boston Red Sox against the New York Yankees in the 2004 AL Championship Series.
“It just shows the resiliency of this group,” Williamson said. “We continue to fight, and that’s been the motto this series and this full season, is just fight.”
Caminero was replaced by Mullins at third base and hobbled off the field with an ailing left foot. But the All-Star slugger said he’ll definitely play Wednesday night.
“He’ll play tomorrow on one leg. I’ll make sure of it,” Cash said.
Tampa Bay ended an eight-game winning streak by the Brewers, who were bidding to become only the second team to sweep a League Championship Series and the World Series.
“I feel like today we’ve just been playing so free,” DeLuca said. “It’s a pretty cool position we’re in and it’s a special opportunity that we have."
David Hamilton also homered for the Brewers. Jackson Chourio had a single and double, improving to 10 for 20 in the Series.
“When you’re achieving something like this, it’s going to have its adversity,” Murphy said. “We had some things go our way yesterday. They had some things go their way today. That’s the way it is.”

Pratt, a 22-year-old who debuted in June, drove a slider into the left-field seats against Seymour to become the first rookie to hit a World Series extra-inning homer. His go-ahead hit sparked the Brewers to a 5-4 win in Game 2 after Seymour allowed Frelick’s tying home run.
“Nobody said this was going to be easy,” Pratt said.
Milwaukee fans in the crowd of 40,514, many waving yellow towels and some wearing cheeseheads, brought a Badger State feel to Tropicana Field.
Tampa Bay returned to its white home jerseys, a day after playing in Devil Rays throwbacks.
Simpson hit an RBI double off starter Dustin May in the second, but Milwaukee tied the score in the fourth against Griffin Jax when Frelick hit a two-out single and came around on Pratt's double.

Caminero singled leading off the bottom half to chase May and advanced on a groundout. DeLuca hit a hard grounder to Hamilton and Caminero twisted toward the grass to avoid the third baseman’s tag, then came home when Hamilton bounced his throw past Bauers for an error.

Hamilton, Milwaukee’s No. 9 hitter, drove an 0-2 fastball at the letters from Jax into the right-field seats for his second home run of the postseason — half his regular-season total and just his second since June 6.

Six scoreless innings followed before the late drama in a 4-hour, 20-minute game that ended at 12:28 a.m. with the first Series walk-off pinch hit in extra innings since Gene Larkin's single won Game 7 for Minnesota in 1991.
“You play Wiffle ball in the backyard with your friends and you’re dreaming of hitting a walk-off ball in the World Series,” Williamson said.

title: Brewers' Aaron Ashby breaks postseason scoreless relief record as World Series Game 4 goes to extras
summary: Milwaukee Brewers left-hander Aaron Ashby broke Andrew Miller’s record for scoreless innings by a reliever in one postseason with a 1-2-3 ninth in Game 4 of the World Series
story: Milwaukee Brewers left-hander Aaron Ashby broke Andrew Miller’s record for scoreless innings by a reliever in one postseason with a 1-2-3 ninth in Game 4 of the World Series

ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. -- Milwaukee Brewers left-hander Aaron Ashby broke Andrew Miller's record for scoreless innings by a reliever in one postseason with a 1-2-3 ninth in Game 4 of the World Series on Tuesday night.

Ashby followed with a scoreless 10th and hasn't allowed a run in 17 2/3 innings in nine postseason appearances. Milwaukee was tied 2-2 with Tampa Bay going into the 11th inning. The Brewers led the series 3-0 and were a victory away from the first World Series title in franchise history.
Ashby, who was 13-3 with a 3.12 ERA in 71 relief appearances during the season, has been untouchable in October. He's allowed five hits, walked three and has 19 strikeouts.

Miller had the longest streak of consecutive scoreless relief innings within one postseason with 16 in 2016 for Cleveland. Including the regular season, Ashby has thrown a career-best 22 2/3 straight scoreless innings.
Ashby had struggled in the postseason before this one. He allowed nine runs — eight earned — in 9 1/3 playoff innings over 10 appearances in 2021, 2024 and 2025.
Brewers relievers have allowed just eight earned runs over 60 2/3 postseason innings.

title: Brewers fans flock to the Trop, eager to celebrate the franchise's first World Series title
summary: Brewers fans are flocking to Tropicana Field in hopes of seeing their team win a World Series title
story: Brewers fans are flocking to Tropicana Field in hopes of seeing their team win a World Series title

ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. -- A large group of Brewers fans gathered in a parking lot outside Tropicana Field more than four hours before the first pitch of Game 4 of the World Series, sipping on Wisconsin beers and preparing for a potentially historic night.
The Brewers needed one more win to celebrate the first World Series title in franchise history.
“We’re ready to party,” a man wearing a pinstriped, white William Contreras No. 24 jersey said.
With Milwaukee leading the Tampa Bay Rays 3-0, a celebration seems inevitable.

Of the 43 previous major league teams to fall behind 3-0 in any best-of-seven postseason series, only the 2004 Boston Red Sox rallied to win four straight games when they beat the New York Yankees in the American League Championship Series.

Brewers fans have been waiting for this moment since 1970 — the franchise began as the Seattle Pilots in 1969 and moved to Milwaukee a year later. Thousands of fans made the trip from Wisconsin to Florida and sat among the cowbell-ringing Rays crowd on Monday night. Most were sitting behind the visitors’ dugout and along the third-base line, and they had plenty to cheer about in a 10-1 victory.

“The atmosphere here with the amount of Brewers fans, you can feel it, and it started in batting practice yesterday,” Milwaukee’s Garrett Mitchell said Tuesday. “Just like when we were stretching, you could hear it. It was lots of ‘Let’s go Brewers’ chants. To have that on the road, pretty special. Pretty special.”
Even more Brewers fans were expected for Game 4 because their team is on the verge of a championship, and the Rays need to defy historical trends just to shift the series back to Milwaukee.
There have been 25 teams that took a 3-0 lead in the World Series. Of those, 21 finished the sweep in Game 4, and the remaining four won the series in Game 5.

The cheapest ticket available for Game 4 was $900, according to ticket marketplace TickPick. A total of 41.3% of all purchases for Game 4 have come from Wisconsin, compared to 30.5% from Florida and 3.4% from Illinois, according to TickPick.

A fan wearing a powder blue, No. 19 Robin Yount jersey held a broomstick in the parking lot, anticipating a sweep. Once the gates opened, there was a loud “Let's go Brewers” chant when players began stretching in left field.

As the stadium began to fill about an hour before the first pitch, it appeared there were more Brewers fans than Rays fans in the stands. They filled the area behind Milwaukee's dugout and screamed when the players walked back to the clubhouse.

“It was awesome,” Brewers captain Christian Yelich said after Game 3. “They were really loud from batting practice on throughout the game. I said it a bunch, but they brought it this year in Milwaukee and on the road. We understand how much this team and our performance affects people’s happiness in Milwaukee and how many memories have been made over the years watching Brewer baseball, watching us play, whether that’s among family, the friends, parents, grandparents, whatever it may be. So, I know this team doesn’t take that lightly and I understand that our team means a lot to people and it’s a big reason why we press so hard about that.”
And for those who didn't make the road trip, American Family Field in Milwaukee sold out a watch party for 31,000 fans.
Milwaukee’s only previous trip to the World Series in 1982 ended in heartbreak when the Brewers blew a 3-1 lead in the sixth inning of Game 7 and lost 6-3 to the St. Louis Cardinals.

Pat Murphy’s team is trying to finish what Harvey Kuenn’s star-studded crew couldn’t accomplish. Harvey’s Wallbangers had five Hall of Famers: Yount, Paul Molitor, Ted Simmons, Don Sutton and Rollie Fingers. But Fingers missed the postseason with a forearm injury. They also had Hall of Famer Bob Uecker in the broadcast booth.

“I think it’s just about the Brewers, it’s about the city of Milwaukee, it’s about the state of Wisconsin all coming together,” Murphy said. “We all play a role. It’s wonderful to all be together. Hopefully we continue to play well enough to win.”

title: Villanova relies on 'power of the pope' going into Rome doubleheader against Notre Dame
summary: Villanova's basketball teams are set to open their season in Italy with a doubleheader against Notre Dame
story: Villanova's basketball teams are set to open their season in Italy with a doubleheader against Notre Dame
VILLANOVA, Pa. -- Kevin Willard and his family have vacationed in Italy often enough that the Villanova coach could probably get a side hustle as a tour guide.

The Catholic coach at the Augustinian university has marveled at the Sistine Chapel — named after Pope Sixtus IV, an art patron who oversaw the construction of the main papal chapel in the 15th century — and other sites he hoped his team could visit ahead of its season-opener in Italy on Sunday.
“If you've never been to the Vatican, you've never been to Rome, it's one of the most unbelievable experiences you could ever go to,” Willard said.
His favorite stop was the Pope Carriage Pavilion, the wing of the Vatican museum that houses centuries of popemobiles and other types of papal transport.

“It was just kind of cool to see the evolution from the early years to where they are now,” Willard said. “Each pope has a different kind of taste. It's the grandeur and some guys didn't have grandeur.”

College basketball is embracing grandeur with the Eternal City Tip-Off, a Villanova-Notre Dame doubleheader in Rome to cap a visit that includes an audience with the Wildcats’ most blessed alumnus: Pope Leo XIV.

The men's teams play first on Fox — the network is eliminating one of its NFL pregame shows to make room on the slate — and the women's game follows on FS1. Tip-off for the men’s game is at 9:30 a.m. ET on Sunday and the women follow at noon.

College basketball has made strides over the last few years in trying to open the season with a bang and grab casual fans' attention well before March. That includes a wave of high-profile matchups such as Duke at Kansas in an exhibition game meant to whet the appetite for the Eternal City Tip-Off and other games like it.

Health permitting, the pope is scheduled to hold a private audience on Saturday with all four teams and their traveling fans. A total of about 7,000 people are expected in the Paul VI audience hall inside the Vatican.

“Yeah, it just makes it that much better,” Notre Dame point guard Braeden Smith said when asked about visiting the pope. “It’s a great opportunity for us. To be able to travel with your teammates is also a great opportunity and get make some new memories together."
A series of events in Italy includes everything from a welcome reception for fans, a basketball clinic for area children and a private mass celebrated by Archbishop Nelson J. Pérez.

“There's a balance because it's not like a summer tour,” Willard said. “It's still understanding that the season is in front of us. It's just too important of a trip and an experience not to give them the time and opportunity to go see stuff.”
The plans involving the pope were made before the 71-year-old Leo had the lower lobe of his right lung removed earlier this month and was diagnosed with lung cancer.

“I'm Catholic and I take my faith seriously,” Willard said. “If we were able to meet the leader of the Catholic Church, it's a pretty special experience. Even if I wasn't Catholic, I still think it would be an unbelievable experience.”
The men’s game will mark a Villanova debut on home soil for 7-foot-3 freshman center Luigi Suigo, a 19-year-old from Tradate, Varese who is a projected NBA draft lottery pick.
“The only thing I miss about home is my food,” Suigo said. “That's it. I like to be here.”

Villanova was picked to finish second in the Big East preseason women's poll. Coach Denise Dillon knows her Wildcats could use a helping hand in beating No. 13 Notre Dame beyond the play of guards Jasmine Bascoe and Kennedy Henry.
“We'll rely on the power of the pope,” Dillon said.
The Chicago-born pope said in a September trip on his plane that the “the voice of the people of God” will be cheering loudly for Villanova University.
“They tell me that the people coming to the match, 90% are Villanova and 10% Notre Dame, so the voice of the people of God will be very strong on the Villanova side,” Leo said.
Maybe that could explain some of the college basketball versions of a miracle that have crossed over to Villanova.

The 1985 Wildcats are still the lowest-seeded team — eighth — to ever win a national basketball championship. Was there help from above when Kris Jenkins sank his March Madness buzzer-beating 3-pointer to win the 2016 national title against North Carolina?
The Fighting Irish have won two women's championships (2001, 2018) but the men are still looking for an NCAA title.
Irish swingman Ethan Roberts said only a few schools would get the chance to play in Rome.

“I think it speaks to the brand ... who else would get this opportunity outside of a few schools, Notre Dame being one of them?" he said. "But it’s just so exciting, you know. Starting there is incredible.”

title: After a basketball-free summer, All-American Strong returns to lead No. 2 UConn on and off the court
summary: Sarah Strong was a key factor in UConn winning the national championship as a freshman and was the AP Player of the Year during her sophomore year
story: Sarah Strong was a key factor in UConn winning the national championship as a freshman and was the AP Player of the Year during her sophomore year
STORRS, Conn. -- Sarah Strong thought about the question for a few moments and couldn’t remember having a summer quite like the one she just experienced.

There were no games to play, practices to refine her skills. As a daughter of two professional athletes, basketball dominated Strong’s summers for as long as the preseason AP All-American can remember.

Eager to get fully healthy after rarely practicing during the Huskies’ run to the 2026 Final Four, Strong stayed away from the court. When she got back to playing basketball, she felt reenergized heading into her junior year.

“It helped me health-wise; I think mentally it was good to get a break from playing basketball and working out all the time,” Strong said. “I think I was able to see my family and friends and just kind of be present all the time.”
Now, she is ready to lead second-ranked UConn back to the top after a loss in the Final Four last spring spoiled a championship repeat bid.

Strong is the only player in UConn women’s basketball storied history with at least 1,000 points, 600 rebounds, 250 assists, 200 steals, 100 blocked shots and 100 3-pointers by the end of her sophomore season.
It’s not all about the numbers. Strong is driven by team success. She was a pivotal piece of everything the Huskies did the last two seasons alongside stars like Paige Bueckers and Azzi Fudd.
This is her show now.

“(When) Sarah decides to say something, no matter what it is, it is quiet and they listen,” UConn coach Geno Auriemma said. “The more she takes advantage of that, the better it is for us. She has been doing that. We had a long conversation in June about what that looks like, what that means. I think when you are a freshman or sophomore, you go, ‘I don’t want to step on anybody’s toes or get in their way.’ I think there comes a point where you can’t worry about that stuff. I like the direction that she is going.”
Making shots, setting up teammates and grabbing rebounds looks so easy for Strong. This year, her voice is essential if the Huskies want to make another title run.

“She definitely has grown so much since her freshman year,” senior guard Ashlynn Shade said. “I think she is just so comfortable in a leadership role, being honest with people, being a vocal leader and helping people out. Obviously, her basketball speaks for herself; that is never going to go away. She is Sarah, she can do anything. You definitely see her stepping up and wanting to push us, wanting to hold us accountable and it has been really good to see it.”

Bueckers led the team that won the national title when Strong was a freshman. Last year, Fudd took on that role. Strong plans on using what she learned from the last two WNBA No. 1 overall picks, but doing things her way.

“It just takes time,” Strong said. “I think I will be more comfortable with it as the season goes on. We just started but I will continue to get better at it in the next year and whatever I have left. I am not Paige; I am going to do it my own way. I can’t really do what she did; I just have to do what I feel comfortable doing and it is going to take time.
“I think it is important because if I am not going to do it, it is not going to happen. I have to fit into that role and start being comfortable with that.”

Perhaps nobody understands what Strong is about to embark on more than UConn assistant coach Nykesha Sales, a dynamic freshman on UConn’s first national championship team. By the time she was a junior, she was asked to be more vocal and take ownership following the graduation of some All-Americans.

“It’s probably the same storyline, to be honest," Sales said. "She came in and won a championship; I came in and won a championship. Now the big dogs leave so you have to not only still produce what you did as a freshman and sophomore, but now you have to be way more vocal. She is a quiet person. I noticed she likes to play, but now she is being more vocal, which will help her career moving forward.”

title: Kathy Behrens, who developed NBA Cares, plans to leave the league office after a 26-year run
summary: Kathy Behrens, one of the highest-ranking female executives in the NBA, has decided to leave her position after 26 years
story: Kathy Behrens, one of the highest-ranking female executives in the NBA, has decided to leave her position after 26 years

Kathy Behrens started her high school basketball career at a time when her home state of New York had yet to even start a championship for girls. She played in college, long before the women’s game had the immense following it does now. And the WNBA had not even been dreamed of in those days.
Basketball became her life's work anyway.

Behrens — who became one of the highest-ranking women in the NBA office, holding her current title of President of Social Responsibility and Player Programs since 2015 — has decided to leave the league office after 26 years. Colleagues were informed on Tuesday, and she intends to depart at the end of the year.

“Last year I celebrated my 25th year at the NBA and my kids went off to college and I’ve spent the last year thinking about how it’s such a hard place to leave because it’s been just an incredible experience,” Behrens said in an interview with The Associated Press. “And the work is great and so meaningful. I love the people that I work with. But I had just started to think that it’s time to do some other things. It’s that time.”

Among her best-known accomplishments: She developed the wildly successful NBA Cares program, which has long been a top priority for the league in terms of community outreach, as well as oversaw the creations of the NBA Foundation and the National Basketball Social Justice Coalition during the pandemic.
Commissioner Adam Silver lauded Behrens on Tuesday for what he called “an extraordinary NBA career.”

“Kathy has supported generations of players in navigating the demands of their careers, developing interests beyond basketball and preparing for life after the game,” Silver said in a memo distributed to staff, a copy of which was obtained by the AP. “Throughout her career, Kathy has been a trusted colleague and friend and a passionate advocate for basketball’s ability to improve lives, and I am deeply grateful for everything Kathy has done for our leagues.”
In college, Behrens studied education but developed a fascination with politics and was president of Hartford’s student government. She figured that would be her career path.

After graduating, she worked for the United Way in New York as a fundraiser, then got asked to join Gov. Mario Cuomo’s administration. She worked for Cuomo for more than six years, and when he lost a bid for what would have been a fourth term in 1994 Behrens found herself looking for a new challenge.

She became executive director of a nonprofit program called New York Cares. In 1998, that organization worked with the NBA on events related to that year’s All-Star Game in New York. And a couple of years later, Behrens was asked to join the league office — which is when she started getting to know then-Commissioner David Stern.

“To me, David was sort of like the Mario Cuomo of the sports world,” Behrens said. “My final interview was with David, Adam and (then-deputy commissioner) Russ Granik. I thought I’d died and gone to heaven. I have always remained so grateful for the privilege to work around the game, to be connected to the game and contribute to the success and the growth that we’ve had.”

The name “NBA Cares” is a nod to New York Cares. Stern pushed for the name, and Behrens initially felt like it was too close to the name of her past employer. But in time, she, Stern and Silver realized it was the perfect moniker. The program officially launched in 2005, has seen NBA personnel give more than 6.5 million hours of their time to various causes and has generated hundreds of millions of dollars to groups that needed the support.
“It made sense and it clicked,” Behrens said. “We launched it and the enduring legacy of that is something I’m incredibly proud of.”

The decision to step away, she insists, was not easy. For a quarter-century or so now, Behrens has had a little tradition of standing with Dan Rube, one of the league’s executive vice presidents and general counsel, at an NBA Finals game. They always say the same thing, reminding each other to never take being part of the NBA for granted.
“It was a gift and it makes it hard to leave,” Behrens said. “But it’s time to give the gift to other people.”

title: LIV Golf's future and the ripple effect for PGA and European tours provide plenty of drama
summary: The suspense around LIV Golf is greater in court than it ever was on the golf course
story: The suspense around LIV Golf is greater in court than it ever was on the golf course

LIV Golf didn't generate this much suspense at tournaments when the music was blaring, the Saudi cash was flowing freely and players from the Cleeks and Majestics headed off in carts for the shotgun start.
Every day, there's more speculation. Who's leaving? Who's staying? Weren't these the same questions four years ago?

It was May 31, 2022, when a group of golf writers out to dinner in Ohio received emails announcing the field for the inaugural LIV Golf event — Dustin Johnson and 12 other PGA Tour members — and had to leave before the creme brulee arrived.
And now another waiting game, not for the launch but whether LIV survives.

LIV Golf is working through Chapter 11 bankruptcy with a pledge of $300 million from BC Partners Credit, a far cry from the $5 billion the Public Investment Fund of Saudi Arabia dropped in four years before abruptly pulling the plug.

Key to the “LIV 2.0” version — at least 10 tournaments, player equity and prize money half of what it used to be — is getting a “critical mass” of players to buy into the plan. How many players comprise a critical mass is unclear. And while LIV officials don't plan to announce each decision piecemeal, players are doing that for them.

Jon Rahm and Sergio Garcia have court-approved separations from LIV and are free to go. Louis Oosthuizen, Ian Poulter, Tom McKibbin and Adrian Meronk have said they are leaving. Graeme McDowell added his name to the list Monday with a succinct message on social media.

Adding a wrinkle to the immediate future of LIV was a report by The Athletic that Johnson was among more than 10 players seeking severance deals from PIF worth more than $100 million in contract payments. Johnson's attorney suggested a deal was tied to players sticking with LIV 2.0.
“The decision to release potential claims against the PIF and join LIV 2.0 will be influenced largely by how the PIF manages the windup of LIV 1.0," David Cornwell told The Athletic.

An amended restructuring agreement approved by the New Jersey bankruptcy court indicates LIV no longer has a hard deadline for players to decide. The hope was to have a decision by the end of the month. LIV remains bullish about a 2027 season.
That won't be the end of the drama, however, and it would seem the golf landscape is still a long way off from being stitched back together, if it ever can be.

The PGA Tour has yet to say whether defectors — currently banned for one year from the date of their last LIV appearance — have a place. It's not a high priority as the tour seeks to fill out its lucrative “Championship Series” schedule in 2028 and find sponsors for the second tier.
The European tour, meanwhile, delivered a strong ultimatum when CEO Guy Kinnings said anyone staying with LIV need not apply for membership for the commercially known DP World Tour.

That made it an easy choice for Rahm and Tyrrell Hatton — particularly with Ryder Cup strings attached — and for youngsters Tom McKibbin and David Puig. They have status based on performance. That doesn't mean it sits well with those who stayed.

“Four years ago, they didn't give a (crap) about the DP World Tour,” Joost Luiten told Today's Golfer. “They made a decision to go after the money. And now all of a sudden, the money is gone and they want to come back and act like nothing happened. I don’t think that’s right.”
There's also the matter of sponsor exemptions for those who don't have status, or even those who never gave much thought to the European tour because they didn't need it. Now they do.
European tour officials are not in position to turn their back on a chance to strengthen fields.

“Given the high volume of inbound interest and enquiries we have received in recent weeks, we are exploring the terms on which we are willing to accommodate players provided they are free from third party contractual restrictions and are willing to abide by our membership regulations,” a European tour spokesman said.

It's possible such players are allowed only a set number of exemptions. And because the exemptions are for stock events — think Magical Kenya Open and the Soudal Open in Belgium — it might not be a case of squeezing out a more worthy player.
But then it's a matter of whether loyalty means more than name recognition.

Eddie Pepperell, among the most thoughtful players, missed the cut last week in South Korea and wound up one spot out of a full European tour card for 2027. He wrote in his “The Chipping Forecast” post that outside of players whom people pay to watch, send everyone else to Q-school.
But potentially losing a spot in the field to a player no longer interested in LIV because it no longer offers $20 million purses with no cuts?

“As someone who has gone through the wringer this game provides (mostly due to my own shortcomings of course) in recent years, and who has gone back to Q School and had two immensely divergent experiences, betrayal feels like the right word,” Pepperell wrote. “And unfortunately when one feels that way inevitably what follows is a loss of respect, and what tends to fill the void left behind is resentment and contempt.”
No matter what happens to LIV, one suspects it won't make the healing process any easier.

title: French soccer league moves games from Saturday amid public protests on streets
summary: The French soccer league is moving scheduled games from Saturday at the request of public authorities amid weekend protests across the country
story: The French soccer league is moving scheduled games from Saturday at the request of public authorities amid weekend protests across the country
PARIS -- The French soccer league is moving scheduled games from Saturday at the request of public authorities amid weekend protests across the country.

Lyon’s home game against Angers in Ligue 1 will now be played on Sunday afternoon instead of 8:45 p.m. local time on Saturday, the Professional Football League (LFP) said Tuesday in a statement citing a request from local government officials.
Ligue 1 games to be hosted Saturday by Nice and Lorient have also been changed to, respectively, Friday evening and Monday evening, the league said.
Hundreds of thousands of people took part in marches across France last Saturday to protest rising living costs and poor conditions in schools, adding to demands on police and security forces.
France’s worst civil unrest for years has seen city halls and public buildings attacked.

title: Naomi Osaka advances to 2nd round in front of home fans in Tokyo
summary: Naomi Osaka has defeated Italy’s Jasmine Paolini in front of her home fans at the Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo
story: Naomi Osaka has defeated Italy’s Jasmine Paolini in front of her home fans at the Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo

TOKYO -- Naomi Osaka defeated Italy’s Jasmine Paolini in front of her home fans at the Pan Pacific Open on Tuesday, winning 6-3, 7-6 (4) to advance to the second round of the WTA 500-level event in Tokyo.
The victory for Osaka — seeded No. 7 — avenges her loss to Paolini last year in the Miami Open, their only previous meeting.
The 29-year-old Osaka racked up seven aces to only one for Paolini in a match that lasted 1 hour and 37 minutes.
The four-time Grand Slam champion is playing some of her best tennis since returning after giving birth three years ago to her daughter, Shai.
But Osaka said this week that she would step away from the game if Shai asked her to.
Elena Rybakina is seeded No. 1 — she is also the WTA's top-ranked player — and had a bye in the first round.
Two top players have pulled out with injuries: No. 2 Maja Chawlinska and No. 4 Belinda Bencic.

title: Venus Williams 0-13 in singles this year after losing to rival 28 years younger at Guangzhou Open
summary: Tennis great Venus Williams has fallen to 0-13 in singles matches this year at age 46
story: Tennis great Venus Williams has fallen to 0-13 in singles matches this year at age 46
GUANGZHOU, China -- Tennis great Venus Williams fell to 0-13 in singles matches this year at age 46 after losing 6-2, 6-2 to teenager Lilli Tagger in the Guangzhou Open first round on Tuesday.
Their 28-year age gap was reportedly a record difference between opponents in a WTA Tour match.
The 18-year-old Austrian Tagger was born in 2008, the year Williams won the last of her seven Grand Slam singles titles at Wimbledon.
Now ranked No. 599, Williams was playing her first singles match for two months since the U.S. Open, where she lost in the first round to Sofia Kenin.
Williams now has lost 16 straight singles matches on tour going back to July last year.
She matched the 53rd-ranked Tagger with each landing 63% of their first serves, though Williams won just 60% of those points and her opponent won all of hers.
Williams created no break-point chances and Tagger took four of the 16 she had.
Kenin also lost her round of 32 match, beaten 6-4, 6-7 (5), 6-4 by Kaitlin Quevedo.
