title: GOP Senate majority faces fresh uncertainty as 2 key races tighten days before midterms
summary: Sherrod Brown leads Jon Husted within the margin of error in Ohio while Darline Graham and Annie Andrews are tied in South Carolina polling.
story: Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., calls Ohio "ground zero" for crucial midterm election while campaigning with Republican Senate nominee Jon Husted on Tuesday, Oct. 27.

Two of the country’s most watched Senate races, in Ohio and South Carolina, remain neck and neck with under a week to go until the Nov. 3 midterm elections, polling results released on Wednesday show.

In both states, the tight margins are a welcome sign for Democrats as they try to unseat a pair of Republican incumbents: Sen. Jon Husted, R-Ohio, and Sen. Darline Graham, R-S.C. Should both races go their way, Democrats would find themselves within striking distance of eliminating the current 53-seat Republican majority in the Senate.
Ohio: Within the Margin of Error
Democratic Senate candidate, U.S. Sen. Sherrod Brown, D-Ohio, addresses volunteers at a campaign office on November 4, 2024, in Cleveland Heights, Ohio. (Stephen Maturen/Getty Images)
FOX NEWS POLL: GENDER GAP AND POCKETBOOK PAIN SHAPE OHIO SENATE RACE

In Ohio, findings from Suffolk University show Democratic nominee Sherrod Brown leading Sen. Jon Husted, R-Ohio, 47% to 44%. The poll has a margin of error of plus or minus 4.4 percentage points, putting the race within the margin of error. Four percent of voters were undecided, while 3% backed another candidate.
Brown, a former senator who lost his seat in 2024, is trying to make a political comeback, pitching himself as a familiar face amid public frustration with the cost of living.

Throughout his campaign, he has highlighted his career as a policymaker, promising to bring that expertise to issues like affordability and data center expansion. Before losing his seat to Sen. Bernie Moreno, R-Ohio, Brown represented Ohio from 2007 to 2025, chairing the Senate Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs Committee.
South Carolina: Dead Heat
Republican Sen. Darline Graham and Democratic opponent Annie Andrews clashed during a South Carolina U.S. Senate election debate on Oct. 11, 2026. (Courtesy: SCETV)
DARLINE GRAHAM FOCUSES ON KITCHEN-TABLE ISSUES AS SHE ANNOUNCES FULL-TERM SENATE BID

In South Carolina, polling from the Siena Research Institute, in partnership with The New York Times, has found Sen. Darline Graham, R-S.C., in a tie with Annie Andrews, the Democrat in the race, at an even 48% apiece. In that race, 3% of respondents said they were still undecided, while less than 1% said they planned to vote for some third candidate.

Graham, the sister of the late Sen. Lindsey Graham, R-S.C., who was appointed to the seat in July, is looking to secure a full six-year term after beating out a crowded field of Republican challengers in the primary.
Although new to the political scene, Graham has the backing of President Donald Trump and is running in a state that went the president’s way by a 17.8% margin in 2024.
Andrews, Graham’s opponent, has framed her as inexperienced and an extension of Lindsey Graham — one of Trump’s key allies in the Senate.
Sen. Darline Graham, R-S.C., speaks during a campaign event at the Green Boundary Club on Aug. 24, 2026, in Aiken, S.C. (Sean Rayford/Getty Images)

For her own part, Andrews has championed policy positions like enshrining access to abortion, increased requirements for gun ownership and expanding access to healthcare.

title: Democrat's 2-word answer on a possible presidential run draws cheers from Maine crowd
summary: Mark Kelly responded "we'll see" when an audience member shouted "president" during a stump speech, fueling 2028 presidential election speculation.
story: While speaking to a crowd of Troy Jackson supporters in Maine, Sen. Mark Kelly appeared to openly express interest in launching a White House bid.
Sen. Mark Kelly, D-Ariz., appeared to leave the door open for a presidential run in 2028 while giving a stump speech on Tuesday for Troy Jackson, the Democratic nominee for Senate in Maine.
Kelly was in the middle of an argument about how the economy no longer works for young Americans when an audience member interrupted him with a suggestion about his political future.
"I'm the son of two cops who went to public schools and went on to become a Navy pilot and then an astronaut and now a U.S. senator. I was fortunate," he said.
Just as Kelly mentioned becoming a senator, someone in the crowd shouted "president," prompting a two-word response from the Arizona Democrat.

Sen. Mark Kelly, D-Ariz., speaks during a meet-and-greet event held by Kelly and Democratic Senate candidate Troy Jackson ahead of the midterm elections in Freeport, Maine, on Oct. 27, 2026. (Reuters/Taylor Coester)
WATCH: DEM SENATORS DODGE BACKING KAMALA HARRIS IN POTENTIAL 2028 RUN: ‘VERY MESSY’
"We'll see," said Kelly, whose short response drew cheers from the crowd.

Kelly, who is up for re-election in 2028, is routinely featured in 2028 Democratic presidential primary surveys and often polls below more established contenders like former Vice President Kamala Harris and California Gov. Gavin Newsom.

Still, Kelly has begun gaining support as his national profile rises. He drew widespread attention in Nov. 2025 after appearing in a video alongside other Democratic lawmakers telling U.S. service members that it is their duty to disobey illegal orders, including those issued by the executive branch.
The video prompted a criminal investigation into Kelly and the five other Democratic lawmakers, although a federal grand jury declined to indict them in February.
HARRIS KEEPS 2028 DOOR OPEN AS SHE HITS MIDTERM CAMPAIGN TRAIL, WARNS ‘28 WON’T MATTER’ WITHOUT 2026
Axios reported last week that Kelly is eyeing a run for the White House. He told the outlet that he will decide whether he is running for president or another term in the Senate after the midterms.

However, Kelly would not necessarily have to choose between the two. Under Arizona law, presidential and vice presidential candidates are permitted to simultaneously seek election to one additional federal office, meaning Kelly could run for both president and Senate in 2028.
Sen. Mark Kelly, D-Ariz., greets a supporter at a campaign event for Senate candidate Troy Jackson in Freeport, Maine, on Oct. 27, 2026. (Joseph Prezioso/AFP via Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

The provision in Arizona law could make a presidential bid less of a political gamble for Kelly, allowing him to pursue the highest office in the land without necessarily jeopardizing his Senate career.

If Kelly secures the Democratic presidential nomination in 2028, he could appear on Arizona ballots as a candidate for both president and the Senate, though he wouldn't be able to occupy both offices if he won both races.
James Cirrone is a writer on the Breaking/Trending News team at Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to james.cirrone@fox.com.

title: Long-running embassy fight comes back to haunt Trump as State Dept hit with $461M lawsuit
summary: B.L. Harbert International alleges the State Department reached a $370 million settlement over COVID-19 embassy construction claims, then reversed course.
story: Subcontractors on the $1 billion Obama Presidential Center project face severe financial distress, with some alleging they are owed millions in unpaid balances. Mike Owen, president of Adamson Plumbing, reveals substantial losses due to unexpected project delays, while many other businesses are reportedly silenced by non-disclosure agreements.

FIRST ON FOX — The latest lawsuit launched against the Trump administration seeks to recover more than $461 million after the State Department directed a longtime embassy builder to continue construction projects worldwide through the COVID-19 pandemic.

B.L. Harbert International, which has built dozens of U.S. embassies and consulates over more than two decades, reached a $370 million settlement with the State Department to handle resulting claims — but the compnay claims the deal was reversed after current political leadership intervened.

The builders are now seeking to recover lost funding through suing the Trump administration, and filed a lawsuit on Wednesday in the U.S. Court of Federal Claims, Fox News Digital first learned. The complaint covers 12 diplomatic construction projects across four continents, including facilities in Turkey, Iraq, Thailand, Morocco, Mexico and Central America.

The company alleges career State Department officials reached the $370 million agreement in September 2025, but the government paid just $501,636 before backing out. Harbert claims political leadership "inserted themselves into the process after a settlement was reached" and that the decision to abandon it "came from the top."

"We did not want to take this step. The U.S. Government is an important partner, and we are proud of the work we do together to advance America's interests and protect Americans serving overseas," Charles Bohn, president of BL Harbert's International Group, said in a statement.
TRUMP ADMINISTRATION UNCOVERS $1.2B IN SUSPECTED COVID CONTRACT FRAUD TIED TO BIDEN-ERA SPENDING

"But we have a responsibility to our employees and to the future of that mission. We kept our commitment under extraordinarily difficult conditions. We are asking the government to keep its commitment to us."

Six U.S. diplomatic compounds built by B.L. Harbert International and included among the projects at issue in the company's lawsuit against the federal government. (U.S. Court of Federal Claims/B.L. Harbert International)

Harbert is one of a small pool of U.S. contractors capable of building highly secure diplomatic facilities overseas — work that requires specialized security clearances, vetted workforces and the ability to manage complex construction and supply chains abroad. According to the company, some State Department embassy projects now draw just two or three qualified bidders.

The dispute stretches across three presidential administrations, beginning with State Department directives issued during Trump's first term in 2020, continuing as Harbert pursued compensation during the Biden administration and culminating in the alleged settlement and its collapse during Trump's second term.

At the beginning of the Covid-19 pandemic, Harbert was working on 17 embassy and consulate construction projects around the world, representing nearly two-thirds of State's embassy construction program at the time, according to the lawsuit.

As countries shut down and global supply chains seized up in early 2020, Harbert says it sought guidance from State on whether to pause construction. The company argues the pandemic constituted an "excusable delay" under its contracts that would have allowed it to send personnel home, secure construction sites and resume work once conditions stabilized.
Instead, Harbert alleges State decided to keep its overseas construction program moving.

The company says State directed it to remain ready to mobilize, continue procuring and shipping materials and work through the disruptions, while instructing Harbert to document the resulting costs and submit requests for reimbursement.

In one March 2020 communication cited in the complaint, Harbert warned State that it could not afford to continue paying workers to remain on standby without assurances of reimbursement. Labor costs on the new U.S. Embassy in Guatemala City alone were running roughly $1.3 million per month, according to the filing.
Former military protest outside the US Embassy in Guatemala City on June 26, 2024. (JOHAN ORDONEZ/AFP via Getty Images)

Weeks later, State directed Harbert to "continue to procure and ship materials" so projects would not end up at the "back of the line" when global construction activity resumed, the complaint alleges. State recognized that doing so could generate additional storage, shipping and other costs and directed the company to submit requests for equitable adjustments as those costs arose, according to the filing.

The projects ultimately moved forward under pandemic restrictions that Harbert says increased costs and reduced productivity as the company dealt with workforce limitations, supply-chain disruptions and new operating requirements.
The government has since taken possession of all 12 diplomatic facilities at issue in the lawsuit and has been using some of them for more than three years, according to Harbert.

Harbert ultimately submitted more than $500 million in requests for equitable adjustments and other claims stemming from the pandemic directives and separate project disputes, including alleged design changes and government-caused delays.
OBAMA CENTER SUBCONTRACTOR SHUTS DOWN AMID $4M FIGHT, LAYS OFF 25

Harbert alleges members of State Department political leadership "inserted themselves into the process after a settlement was reached" and that, "on information and belief," the decision to abandon the agreement "came from the top."
Fox News Digital has reached out to the State Department for comment.

With deadlines approaching to preserve its claims, Harbert says it formally certified them in March 2026. The complaint alleges State's chief of staff encouraged the company to do so, representing that certification would make it easier for the government to implement the settlement.
Instead, State contracting officers began denying the claims in July. By Oct. 13, 2026, all 13 certified claims now at issue in the lawsuit had received final decisions.
This picture taken on May 21,2026 shows a general view of the US embassy building in Ankara. (Getty Images)
Harbert is now seeking at least $461,097,380 in damages, along with interest and other relief.

The lawsuit does not currently ask the court to enforce the alleged $370 million settlement itself. Harbert says its settlement-related claims remain in the administrative process and that it reserves the right to add them to the lawsuit later.
The dispute could carry consequences beyond the hundreds of millions of dollars at stake.

Harbert has been awarded roughly 60 U.S. embassy and consulate construction projects since 1999. The company says the number of American contractors willing and qualified to undertake such work has dwindled significantly, in some cases leaving just two or three qualified bidders for projects.

Embassy construction requires contractors to meet stringent security and workforce-vetting requirements while managing highly specialized construction, secure facilities and international logistics, creating significant barriers for companies seeking to enter the field.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Harbert argues that if contractors lose confidence that State will honor its obligations, fewer could be willing to take on the work, further shrinking the government's options for constructing secure diplomatic facilities overseas.

title: Trump revisits 10-year warning to Macron as protests sweep France: ‘You have to get them out’
summary: Donald Trump told Emmanuel Macron for a decade that France would "lose" its country without addressing the immigration crisis fueling protests.
story: President Donald Trump told Fox News Digital that France’s unrest is an "immigration problem," warning the country must do something about it.
President Donald Trump revisited his longstanding warning to French President Emmanuel Macron that France could "lose" its country if it doesn’t address immigration troubles.
"It's not a school problem. It's an immigration problem," Trump told Fox News Digital Tuesday night after rallying in Texas in a final push for Republicans ahead of next week's midterms.
"I've been saying that to President Macron for a long time, who I like a lot, by the way. But I said, ‘You're going to end up losing your country if you don't do something.’"

Trump’s call for France to close its borders follows student demonstrations that have devolved into widespread protests over local grievances, packing streets, sparking clashes and ricocheting across Europe.
TRUMP REVEALS DIRE WARNING TO MACRON AS VIOLENT UNREST SPREADS ACROSS EUROPE

President Donald Trump (right) takes part in the Gaza summit chaired by Egypt’s President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi alongside France’s President Emmanuel Macron in Sharm el-Sheikh, Egypt, on Oct. 14, 2025. (Michael Kappeler/Picture Alliance via Getty Images)

During a conversation with U.S. Ambassador to France Charles Kushner earlier this week, Trump told Fox News Digital they discussed France’s immigration problems, which he believes were behind the protests.
"You have people that hate France," he said. "They hate the buildings, hate the art, they hate the people. And they're in there, and you have to get them out."
Trump called the situation in France and across Europe "very sad," saying his warnings to Macron have spanned a decade.
"Something has to happen, and they better do something," he said. "I’ve been saying it for 10 years, too."
Trump has raised concerns about immigration in Europe for roughly a decade, dating back to his first presidential campaign in 2016. Macron became France's president in 2017.
VIOLENT FAR-LEFT RIOTS IN FRANCE ARE 'CHILLING WARNING' FOR AMERICANS AT HOME, MIKE JOHNSON SAYS
Students clash with police during ongoing student protest action, in Lyon, central-eastern France, on Oct. 1, 2026. (Alex Martin AFP via Getty Images)
Trump has previously credited his own immigration policies with preventing similar unrest in the U.S.

Macron accused foreign leaders last week of making "unacceptable and even stupid" comments, calling them false claims for political gain. He did not mention Trump or Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu by name — both the U.S. and Israel are in the midst of high-stakes election cycles.

In France, French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said "nearly 1,000 people" were arrested Saturday as nationwide protests resumed. Macron said "ultra-left groups whose aim is to bring down the Republic" are leading the protests and that those organized by "individuals or groups with no legitimate authority" would be banned.
FRANCE'S MACRON BLAMES PROTESTS ON 'ULTRA-LEFT GROUPS WHOSE AIM IS TO BRING DOWN THE REPUBLIC'

A fire burns as police officers in riot gear stand guard during civil unrest in Paris, France, the day after a national day of demonstrations against the cost of living and rising fuel prices on Oct. 18, 2026. (Reuters)

Remaining on high alert, Macron said anyone who loots or damages property will be forced to pay, as tens of thousands of police were deployed. A Fox News Digital investigation identified 50 Antifa groups among nearly 300 groups mobilizing around the protests, as well as a sprawling network of communist, socialist, far-left and anti-Israel groups.
Protests also spiraled in other parts of Europe this month, with violence breaking out in Rome and Albania’s capital, Tirana, where demonstrators set government buildings on fire.

title: China exile-turned-GOP nominee warns socialist surge could give Beijing greater influence in Washington
summary: Lily Tang Williams, a New Hampshire Republican who escaped communist China, warns a Democratic Congress could let Beijing expand its influence in Washington.
story: Controversy surrounds Florida state Rep. Angie Nixon as she faces intense backlash over her comments regarding Cuba's dictatorship.

A congressional nominee who escaped communist China after the Tiananmen Square massacre warned that a Democratic-controlled Congress could create opportunities for Beijing to expand its influence in Washington, threatening U.S. national security.

Lily Tang Williams, the Republican nominee for New Hampshire's 2nd Congressional District, told Fox News Digital that China, a country she believes "wants to bring down the United States," would capitalize on "America’s weakness" if Congress were to be controlled by Democrats in January.

"I fear that the country I love is becoming the country I left," Williams, who is challenging Rep. Maggie Goodlander, D-N.H., told Fox News Digital. "China will be very happy to see Democrats control the House and Senate. The Democrats want open borders, they want to defund police and abolish private property. The Chinese Communist Party (CCP) is looking at this as good news."
CHINA EXPERT WARNS BEIJING WANTS AMERICANS — NOT THE CCP — TO SPREAD ITS MESSAGE
Chinese President Xi Jinping speaks during an international business meeting at The Great Hall of the People on March 28, 2025, in Beijing. (Ken Ishii - Pool/Getty Images)

Williams pointed to a recent Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) trip, claiming that more than a dozen high-ranking members of the organization traveled to China to "produce favorable coverage of China and its regime," as an example of the Chinese government taking advantage of the "vulnerable Democratic Party" to promote itself in the U.S.
"They now share a similar ideology," Williams said.
DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS OF AMERICA NEED TO ACTUALLY MEET THE CHINA THEY CLAIM TO LOVE

title: Talarico rally warmup act calls for abolishing ICE, contrasting Senate hopeful's message
summary: Malik Williams called to abolish ICE and legalize cannabis at a James Talarico rally, despite Talarico's recent denial of supporting that policy.
story: Malik Williams, the Democratic candidate for the U.S. House of Representatives in Texas' 83rd legislative district, called for abolishing Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and for legalizing marijuana to raucous applause during a Tuesday rally for for Senate nominee James Talarico in Lubbock, Texas.

Malik Williams, a Democratic candidate for a seat in Texas' state legislature, called for abolishing Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and for legalizing marijuana during a Tuesday rally for U.S. Senate nominee James Talarico in Lubbock, Texas.

"We can legalize and tax THC and cannabis. We're gonna abolish ICE, we're gonna tax the rich and we're going to get my friend, the next United States senator from the state of Texas, James Talarico, elected!" Williams exclaimed to raucous applause.
Talarico, a Democrat running in a historically Republican state, has shied away from making such direct calls to abolish ICE while on the campaign trail.
During a joint CNN and Jubilee town hall, Talarico directly denied wanting to abolish ICE when asked if he supported the idea.
JAMES TALARICO TORCHES BIDEN BORDER POLICIES IN STUNNING ATTACK AD AS PROGRESSIVE TRIES TO FLIP TEXAS BLUE
State Rep. James Talarico, who is running for U.S. Senate, speaks during a town hall on July 11, 2026, at the Plaza Theatre in El Paso, Texas. (USA Today Network via Reuters Connect)

"No, and I never have," Talarico responded, adding, "We need Immigration and Customs Enforcement in this country, but that's not what we're seeing. What we've seen over the last year is a secret police force, and that's what we don't want in this country."
EXCLUSIVE: RESURFACED VIDEO SHOWS JAMES TALARICO DISCUSSING ‘EXCITING’ OPPORTUNITY TO END ‘OVER-POLICING’
Talarico's recent remarks, however, depart from past comments. In January, during a primary debate with Rep. Jasmine Crockett, D-Texas, Talarico said it was time to "tear down" ICE.

"ICE shot a mother in the face. ICE kidnapped a 5-year-old boy. ICE executed a man in broad daylight on our streets just this morning. It's time to tear down this secret police force and replace it with an agency that actually is going to focus on public safety," he said.
FOX NEWS POLL: MAJORITY SAYS IMMIGRATION ENFORCEMENT HAS CROSSED THE LINE
Talarico also advocated for "hauling in" agents in front of Congress to testify on actions taken during enforcement actions.

State Rep. James Talarico and Rep. Jasmine Crockett, both Democratic Senate candidates, debate during the 2026 Texas AFL-CIO COPE Convention in Georgetown, Texas, on Jan. 24. (Bob Daemmrich/The Texas Tribune/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Abolishing ICE is an unpopular opinion among Republicans nationwide, with 67% strongly opposing the idea, according to a July YouGov/The Economist poll. The same poll found 48% of Americans overall supporting ICE's abolition.
TRUMP WON THIS RELIABLY RED STATE BY DOUBLE DIGITS. NOW A DEADLOCKED RACE IS BRINGING HIM BACK

People protest against Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers on Sept. 20, 2026, in Austin, Texas. A federal ICE officer shot and wounded a person earlier in the day in North Austin. (Brandon Bell/Getty Images)

In introducing Talarico on Tuesday, Williams also stumped for a wide number of policies popular with the rising crop of democratic socialists while appearing to bash President Donald Trump and Talarico's Republican opponent Ken Paxton.
DEMOCRATS CAN TAKE THE LEAD ON ONE OF THE NATION’S TOP ISSUES – DATA CENTERS

When the backbone of Texas, our ranchers and farmers, tell us that they do not want data centers and then our politicians, as they love to do, they force it upon us without consent, I say we deserve better!" Williams exclaimed to fanfare.

Malik Williams is the Democratic Party's nominee to represent state House District 83. James Talarico was at the rally at the Fiesta Center in Lubbock, Texas on Tuesday, Oct. 27, 2026. (USA Today Network via Reuters Connect)

title: Trump's unusual legal gambit against Biden-era deportation rule pays off at Supreme Court
summary: The Supreme Court allowed a Texas-DOJ agreement ending the Biden-era administrative closure rule that let judges delay deportation proceedings.
story: New York City sanctuary laws are upheld after a federal judge dismisses a Department of Justice lawsuit, drawing sharp criticism from Joe Abraham, whose daughter Katie was killed in a hit-and-run crash. Meanwhile, New York Gov. Kathy Hochul deflects questions on migrant crime during a gubernatorial debate.
The Supreme Court, with no noted dissents, has allowed an agreement between Texas and the Department of Justice ending a Biden-era immigration rule to go into effect.

The Biden administration adopted the rule in 2024, formally establishing procedures for immigration judges to temporarily pause certain deportation proceedings through a practice known as "administrative closure," including when migrants were pursuing immigration relief through other federal proceedings. The Supreme Court's move leaves in place a lower court ruling eliminating that rule, stripping away a procedure that allowed certain deportation cases to be put on hold.
Texas sued the federal government in June, arguing that the rule was adopted without proper legal authority.
The Department of Justice agreed with Texas, asking the judge overseeing the case to vacate the rule and prevent similar rules from being adopted in the future.
JUDGE WHO APOLOGIZED TO ACCUSED WOULD-BE TRUMP ASSASSIN LIGHTS UP DOJ IN HUNTER BIDEN FBI CASE
The Texas state flag flies alongside the logo from the U.S. Department of Justice. (Getty Images/DOJ)
Opponents accused Texas and the Justice Department of colluding to eliminate the Biden-era rule, arguing that the two sides worked together despite being on opposite sides of the lawsuit.
On the same day the DOJ made its request, District Judge Reed O’Connor, an appointee of President George W. Bush, granted it.
TRUMP-APPOINTED JUDGE SLAMS DOOR ON DOJ AS COURT LOSSES PILE UP DAYS AHEAD OF MIDTERMS'

Texas Gov. Greg Abbott, a Republican, said his working relationship with President Donald Trump is based on their shared belief in public safety. (Shelby Tauber/Bloomberg via Getty Images; Andrew Harnik/Getty Images)

In August, however, three cities with large immigrant populations — Baltimore, Maryland; New Haven, Connecticut; and Columbus, Ohio — joined with Centro Legal de la Raza, an immigrant legal advocacy group, in an effort to intervene in the case and defend the Biden-era rule on appeal.

The cities argued that eliminating the rule could lead to residents being deported, reducing their tax revenues and giving them legal standing to challenge the agreement. O’Connor rejected that argument.
MAMDANI BLASTS FEDS FOR WAGING 'CAMPAIGN OF VIOLENCE AND TERROR' AGAINST NYC'S IMMIGRANTS

President Donald Trump, first lady Melania Trump and Texas Governor Greg Abbott participate in a roundtable event at the Hill Country Youth Event Center on July 11, 2025, in Kerrville, Texas. (Photo by Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images)

On Oct. 9, the three cities and Centro Legal de la Raza asked the Supreme Court to temporarily block the lower court's judgment while their appeal proceeded, accusing Texas and the federal government of engaging in "egregious collusion" to eliminate the Biden-era rule.

Federal lawyers argued that the cities and their allies lacked legal standing to challenge the agreement because they had not demonstrated the concrete injury required for a federal court to consider their claims.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"We are deeply disappointed that the Supreme Court declined to intervene to prevent the Trump-Vance administration from dismantling longstanding immigration court procedures through a backdoor agreement with Texas," the cities and Centro Legal de la Raza said in a statement shared with Fox News Digital.

"For decades, these procedures have allowed immigration judges to temporarily pause deportation proceedings for people pursuing lawful immigration relief, including survivors of violence, abused and neglected children, and victims and witnesses who cooperate with law enforcement," the statement continued. "Eliminating these protections puts vulnerable people at greater risk of deportation and undermines public safety in communities across the country."

title: Mike Collins drops Election Day gas price prediction in heated Georgia Senate race
summary: Republican Rep. Mike Collins details his private conversation with President Trump after the Perry rally and his role in landing Audi's $4.2 billion deal.
story: Georgia Republican Mike Collins jokes about rival's Hollywood makeup artist with Fox News Digital, details his role in $4.2B Audi investment and predicts fuel prices will fall after Election Day.

EXCLUSIVE — Republican Rep. Mike Collins offered a behind-the-scenes look at his latest conversation with President Donald Trump and detailed his role in preparing Georgia's infrastructure for a multibillion-dollar manufacturing investment during an exclusive interview with Fox News Digital on Tuesday, exactly one week before voters decide one of the nation's closely watched Senate contests.

Collins, a trucking company owner challenging Democrat Sen. Jon Ossoff, said he spoke privately with Trump following Saturday's rally in Perry, Georgia, where the president announced a $4.2 billion investment by German automaker Audi.
The Georgia congressman described a president eager to hear feedback from those around him and said he personally relayed what he had observed while meeting rallygoers.
TRUMP SUPPORTERS CONFRONT IRAN, AFFORDABILITY CONCERNS WITH A MESSAGE FOR CRITICS: 'GIVE HIM TIME'

Rep. Mike Collins, the Georgia Republican Senate candidate, speaks alongside President Donald Trump during a midterm campaign rally at the Guardian Centers on Oct. 24, 2026, in Perry, Georgia. (Alex Wong/Getty Images)
"He always wants to know what you think. He wants to know what everybody thinks," Collins told Fox News Digital. "And I think that's just part of his personality."
Collins said he made a point of asking attendees whether they had ever been to a Trump rally before.
"Well over half of the people that were at that event, it was their first time ever attending a Trump rally," Collins said, describing his own conversations with supporters.
The Republican also revealed that Trump helped amplify a new digital advertisement from his Senate campaign focused on the Laken Riley Act, legislation Collins championed in Congress.
TRUMP-BACKED CANDIDATE SURVIVES GRUELING RUNOFF, ADVANCES TO HIGH-STAKES SENATE RACE
President Donald Trump speaks during a midterm campaign rally at the Guardian Centers on Oct. 24, 2026, in Perry, Georgia. (Alex Wong/Getty Images)
"When he saw the ad, he retweeted it out there and of course, it has exploded with over 7 million views," Collins said.
The president's involvement comes as Collins seeks to unseat Ossoff in the final days before the Nov. 3 election.
Collins also elaborated on his involvement in improvements to the Port of Brunswick, which he credits with helping position Georgia to attract Audi's newly announced manufacturing investment.
Trump announced Saturday that Audi would invest $4.2 billion in a new facility in the Macon area, with plans to manufacture approximately 200,000 vehicles annually.
Collins said that after becoming chairman of the House Water Resources and Environment Subcommittee in 2025, he made the Port of Brunswick one of his first priorities.
"Got down there and, lo and behold, that thing has not been fully dredged in over 10 years," Collins said. "Took me about three months, got the money, got it dredged. Now it is fully dredged."

According to Collins, insufficient channel depth had limited what cargo vessels could transport through the port. He argued that improving the port's capacity helped make Georgia more attractive to automakers looking to manufacture and export vehicles.
"One of the reasons that they picked Georgia was because that port is ready to go down there," Collins said.
‘MISLEADING VOTERS’: OSSOFF WARNS DONORS HE’S FALLING BEHIND DESPITE LEADING SENATE FUNDRAISING

Sen. Jon Ossoff, D-Ga., speaks to members of the media during the opening of the state Democratic Party's South DeKalb field office in Decatur, Georgia, on May 23, 2026. (Elijah Nouvelage/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

The Audi announcement has become a point of contention in the Senate campaign. Ossoff has called for more details about the project, while Collins has pointed to his work on port infrastructure as evidence of his economic development record.
The interview also turned personal when Collins was asked about reports concerning Ossoff's campaign spending on a Hollywood makeup artist.

The Washington Times reported Sept. 26 that Ossoff's campaign had spent nearly $3,000 on hair and makeup during the election cycle, more than any other Senate candidate at the time. The outlet cited Federal Election Commission records showing payments to Georgia makeup artist Stephanie Ponder.
Asked whether he personally wears makeup on the campaign trail, Collins responded with a joke.
"The answer is no, I don't use makeup," Collins said. "Some people might want to suggest I put a bag over my head."
Collins then said political advisors had deliberately changed how Ossoff looks and speaks.
"I can't help it that they hired Pee-wee Herman's makeup artist," Collins said.
The comments followed Trump's own references to the fictional character while criticizing Ossoff at Saturday's rally.

Collins also claimed that Ossoff is positioning himself for a potential 2028 presidential campaign, an allegation he framed as his own interpretation of the senator's voting record, endorsements and fundraising.
Ossoff has campaigned on his work in the Senate, including healthcare, affordability and economic issues, while criticizing Collins' support for Trump's policies.
When asked whether he disagrees with Trump on any issue, Collins pointed to the timing of a potential change involving off-road diesel fuel.
"Probably the only thing I would have, I would have jumped on the off-road diesel quicker to run in trucks," Collins said.
The trucking company owner argued that allowing additional diesel supplies into the transportation market sooner could help reduce prices.
He also predicted that consumers would see lower fuel prices following the election.
"You're gonna see prices come down. It's amazing what Election Day is gonna do," Collins said.
The prediction comes as rising energy costs remain a major issue in the Senate race.
Collins defended Trump's broader economic agenda, arguing that lower taxes, deregulation and domestic manufacturing investment would help households struggling with everyday expenses.
Ossoff, meanwhile, has criticized Trump's tariffs and the economic effects of the war with Iran, arguing that administration policies have contributed to higher costs for Georgia families.
Collins ended the exclusive interview with a confident declaration about the approaching election.
"I'm gonna win this race next week. I'm gonna be your next U.S. senator from Georgia," Collins said.
He added that he would move his work from the House to the Senate while continuing to focus on affordability and economic development.
"We're gonna just pick up that old desk, move it across the rotunda, and continue to deliver," Collins said.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

The election is scheduled for Tuesday, Nov. 3, with early voting in Georgia continuing through Friday, Oct. 30.The Ossoff campaign did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.
Jasmine Baehr is a breaking news writer for Fox News Digital, where she covers politics, the military, legal debates surrounding life and family policy, as well as faith and culture.

title: Thune calls Ohio race 'ground zero' in 'knife fight' for Senate while rallying with Husted
summary: John Thune called Ohio "ground zero" for Senate control, warning that a Democratic majority could lead to a 24-month Trump impeachment trial.
story: Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., calls Ohio "ground zero" for crucial midterm election while campaigning with Republican Senate nominee Jon Husted on Tuesday, Oct. 27.
Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., called Ohio "ground zero" for Senate control during a campaign event with Republican nominee Sen. Jon Husted in Lima, Ohio, on Tuesday night.

Following remarks from Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz, Thune praised Oz's work in rooting out waste, fraud and abuse while insisting that Republicans must hold a Senate majority to allow Oz to continue his work.

"That only happens if Jon Husted gets elected next Tuesday. This is ground zero. It seems like it is a lot of election years we come to Ohio, but this literally is ground zero. This is the firewall in the United States Senate. It's the difference between the next two years, President Trump having to deal with Democrats in Congress, House and Senate, where all you'll be doing is investigations," Thune told the crowd.
SENATE CONTROL IS A COIN FLIP — AND DEMOCRATS’ PATH RUNS THROUGH TRUMP COUNTRY

Top Democrats, including House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., and Rep. Gregory Meeks, D-N.Y., have already signaled an intention to use subpoena power to investigate President Donald Trump and members of his Cabinet.

"When people ask what will we do, my answer is simple. We'll use those tools. We'll act like the Congress," Meeks, the ranking member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, told the Associated Press in September.
HOUSE DEMS PLOT TRUMP INVESTIGATION BLITZ IF THEY SEIZE MAJORITY

Rep. Gregory W. Meeks, D-N.Y., and House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., address a press conference during a visit to Denmark, Copenhagen, on April 25, 2025. (Emil Nicolai Helms/Ritzau Scanpix/AFP via Getty Images)

"Well, that will require a trial, some sort of a trial in the United States Senate. And the only difference between a 24-hour impeachment trial in the Senate and a 24-month impeachment trial is a Republican majority," he said.
DEM MAKING SENATE COMEBACK BID SAYS HE WOULDN'T SUPPORT A TRUMP IMPEACHMENT PUSH

Thune then slammed Husted's Democratic opponent, former Sen. Sherrod Brown, who served as a U.S. senator in Ohio from 2007 until 2025, when he ceded his seat to Republican Bernie Moreno after losing in the 2024 election.

"He proved that to us for 30 years when he was in the Senate, he was a rubber stamp for Chuck Schumer and Nancy Pelosi and Joe Biden. We got to keep Jon Husted in the United States Senate, folks. It is absolutely, absolutely critical," Thune said.
SHERROD BROWN'S 1971 LETTER ARGUED AGAINST RELEASING VIETNAM WAR POWS, PODCAST HOSTS REVEAL
Senate Majority Leader John Thune speaks with Sens. Tim Scott and Jon Husted ahead of a press conference on Capitol Hill, March 21, 2026. (Reuters/Nathan Howard)
Thune continued to sing Husted's praises.

"Jon Husted is as good as they come. He is just a solid, solid human being who is principled, hardworking, smart and solution-oriented. He's getting up every day thinking of things he can do to make Ohio better. He did that when he was here in the state legislature and as lieutenant governor for the state of Ohio. He cut taxes here. Came to Washington, cut taxes there. Allowed you to keep more money in your pocket. Secured the border. We haven't had a person released into the country illegally in 17 months. Think about that, folks," Thune continued.
TRUMP ADMIN MARKS 15 STRAIGHT MONTHS WITH ZERO BORDER RELEASES AS APPREHENSIONS PLUNGE 94%
He closed his remarks by hammering home how crucial it is for Ohioans to get out and vote.

"This is a knife fight, folks. This is a bare knuckles brawl, and all you have to do is turn on your television and see that. But the stakes couldn't be higher, consequences couldn't be greater. It's just so important that we get this done," he concluded.
MAPPED: THE STATES TRUMP AND TOP DEMOCRATS ARE TARGETING BEFORE ELECTION DAY
Senate Majority Leader John Thune speaks at a campaign event for Sen. Jon Husted. (Fox News Channel)
Husted, for his part, reiterated the tight nature of his race, also challenging Republican voters to get to the polls.

"We got work to do because this is going to be a close race. This is going to be a close race," Husted told the crowd. "This is like the fourth quarter of a football game. I can tell you that the other side wants to intimidate us. The other side wants to make you think that we're not going to win. The other side is going to try to make you believe that what you do doesn't matter. What you do does matter. You get into the fourth quarter of a football game, and this is what people try to do. They try to intimidate you the whole game. Everybody has a game plan, but they keep punching you. They keep knocking you down. They want to make you quit. Are they going to make you quit?"
FOX NEWS POLL: ECONOMIC ANXIETY AND CANDIDATE CONCERNS DEFINE OHIO SENATE RACE
A recent Fox News survey of likely Ohio voters showed Brown with a slight lead over Husted, with 52% of respondents saying they'd vote for Brown compared to 47% for Husted.

title: Leftist streamer triggers fury after mocking 'funny' injuries to ICE agents at Ilhan Omar event: ‘Disgusting’
summary: Hasan Piker mocked injured ICE agents during a Minneapolis campaign event with Rep. Ilhan Omar, drawing swift condemnation from conservatives.
story: Far-left streamer Hasan Piker was criticized on social media over comments made about ICE agents during an event with Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn.

Far-left streamer Hasan Piker sparked online controversy after he mocked the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents injured in Operation Metro Surge during a campaign event alongside Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., Monday night.

Recalling his time in Minnesota amid protests over the Trump administration’s federal immigration crackdown, Piker said he thought agents must be "extra racist" to be out in frigid winter temperatures and mocked one of them who was injured as the crowd laughed along.

"We saw a lot of funny compilations as well, you know. A lot of hip bones were broken. 'Officer Martinez down,'" he said while speaking to Democratic socialist and failed Minneapolis mayoral candidate Omar Fateh, who hosted the sold-out Minneapolis event.

Piker has joined several prominent Democrats on their campaign trails, emerging as a polarizing figure within the Democratic Party that some are embracing while others are rejecting. He has made national headlines for past rhetoric, including his claim that "America deserved 9/11," and has faced accusations of antisemitism over his remarks on Israel and Hamas.
ILHAN OMAR'S RADICAL STREAMER ALLY RALLIES WITH EMBATTLED LAWMAKER AFTER DC HOME RAID

Hasan Piker, a streamer and creator, appears during day two of Web Summit Vancouver 2026 at the Vancouver Convention Centre in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada, on May 13, 2026. (Sportsfile via Getty Images)

Rep. Angie Craig, D-Minn., and Sen. People protest against the fatal shooting of Renee Nicole Good by a U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent during a rally outside the Whipple Building on Jan. 8, 2026, in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Tim Evans/Reuters)

Piker, who streams his commentary on Twitch, called Republicans "terrorists" during the event, and Omar referred to the party as the "pedophile protection party."
Conservatives on social media quickly condemned Piker's comments.

"Hasan Piker was asked what stuck with him from Operation Metro Surge in Minneapolis: ‘Funny compilations’ of federal agents being injured," Charlie Kirk Show executive producer Andrew Kolvet posted on X. title: Watchdog accuses DSA candidate of blurring charity, business and campaign: ‘What happened to all that money?’
summary: The NLPC complaint alleges Angie Nixon's Moxie Group nonprofit left $210,000 in spending unaccounted for as she campaigns for Florida Senate.
story: Florida U.S. Senate nominee Angie Nixon hosts a town hall with Disney union workers in Orlando to rally local labor support, promote working-class economic policies, and address key community issues.

The National Legal and Policy Center (NLPC), a conservative government watchdog, filed a complaint on Monday against Angie Nixon, a state legislator and candidate for U.S. Senate in Florida backed by the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), alleging that she may have violated "a number of Florida and federal laws."

The complaint asks authorities to probe whether she used her now-defunct nonprofit, the Moxie Group Inc., to benefit herself. It comes as Nixon wages an uphill race to unseat Sen. Ashley Moody, R-Fla.

Nixon's campaign disputes the characterizations, noting that Nixon's involvement with the nonprofit ended in December 2025 when she resigned as its principal manager. The Moxie Group was initially intended to receive federal tax-exempt contributions for a community project named Café Resistance, a community-oriented bookstore and coffee shop in Jacksonville.

NLPC is asking the Federal Election Commission, the IRS, the U.S. Attorney’s Office and the Florida attorney general to investigate the Moxie Group along four lines: unaccounted-for charitable expenses, overlap between the nonprofit and a for-profit business, whether it solicited donations even after the group was disbanded and whether Nixon’s use of her business space for campaign purposes violates federal campaign restrictions.
DEFEATED PROGRESSIVE ‘SQUAD’ LAWMAKER IN HOT SEAT FOR NON-PROFIT’S MISSING PAPER TRAIL

Democratic U.S. Senate candidate and Florida state Rep. Angie Nixon speaks during a campaign event at the St. John Missionary Baptist Church on Sept. 28, 2026, in Boynton Beach, Florida. Nixon faces incumbent Republican U.S. Sen. Ashley Moody, R-Fla., in the November 3 general election. (Joe Raedle/Getty Images)
According to the Moxie Group’s 2024 reporting, it spent $210,000 with an "other" designation, leaving most of its spending unaccounted for.

"While she itemized some of the charity’s expenses … a whopping $210,000 ... was simply listed as ‘other’ with no description or itemization of what those funds were spent for even though the form requires the charity to ‘list item’ for those ‘other’ expenses. What happened to all that money?" NLPC wrote in its complaint.

Parts of the $210,000 figure have broad descriptions but lack itemization in the 2024 reporting. Two of them under the "other" designation include one $42,560 payment and another $68,304 disbursement, both under "program services." A third, a $3,437 item, is categorized under "management & general."
Outside the "other" category, listed expenses include equipment rentals, insurance, advertising, information technology and fees for non-employees.
The unknowns in the money trail, NLPC contends, are especially important given the overlap between Nixon’s nonprofit and her business — the complaint’s second area of concern.

The document notes that after founding her nonprofit in 2019, Nixon transferred its registration license to her personal for-profit company by the same name — DBA Café Resistance Bookstore and Coffee Shop.
SENATE HOPEFUL'S 'TREADING WATER' NARRATIVE CRUMBLES UNDER $500K CAMPAIGN PAYOUTS TO FAMILY
Florida state Rep. Angie Nixon campaigns during a tour of the Little Havana neighborhood on August 15, 2026, in Miami, Florida. (Joe Raedle/Getty Images)

"Although the charity was ostensibly established to raise funds for a local community bookstore/café, the license for that establishment was transferred to her for-profit The Moxie Group LLC DBA Café Resistance Bookstore and Coffee Shop," the complaint reads.
Third, NLPC questioned whether Nixon raised donations for her nonprofit even after its board of directors voted to disband the group on Dec. 15, 2025.
"It waited over nine months to file Articles of Dissolution with the Florida Secretary of State on Oct. 1, 2026," the group wrote.

The complaint says the Moxie Group did not take down its fundraising site, stating that its contributors were promised "a tax receipt for making a donation," a confirmation for charitable donations. The complaint includes screenshots of the now-archived website.

Fox News Digital is not aware of any specific contributions the Moxie Group may have received that were directed to the nonprofit during that time. Nixon's campaign noted that, because she stepped down as the nonprofit's manager in December 2025 — ahead of the board's disbandment on Dec. 15 — she would not have been involved in any decisions about the group's articles of dissolution or donations received after her resignation.

As its final area of concern, NLPC believes that previously reported accounts of letting the group use its space for campaign events — without some form of payment — would constitute a violation of campaign finance laws.

"It appears that the Café Resistance and Bookstore has been functioning as the candidate’s campaign de facto headquarters or a branch thereof. Indeed, Café Resistance is hosting a phone bank operation on its premises," the complaint states.
According to Nixon’s campaign website, the coffee shop is listed as the location for "Ten toes down Tuesday phonebank," an event scheduled for Tuesday, Oct. 27.

"Let’s go all in for Angie!! Tuesdays can be so fun when we spend them phonebanking for Angie! Together we will call registered voters to remind them that early voting is going on statewide and we need them to vote, now more than ever! Bring your charged-up phone, laptops and/or tablets!" the event’s description reads.
Nixon’s campaign said it has not made payments to Café Resistance and has used only the group’s parking lot. The campaign also noted that Nixon does not own the building.

Even so, NLPC also noted that if any of the funding that had been made as a contribution to the nonprofit had ended up paying for the business’ rent, that could also constitute a campaign finance violation, the group contends.
SENATE REPUBLICAN SETTLES SIX-YEAR-OLD CAMPAIGN BILL AFTER BEING CALLED OUT ON SOCIAL MEDIA

Democratic U.S. Senate candidate, Florida state Rep. Angie Nixon speaks during a visit to the Ball and Chain Cuban restaurant/nightclub as she campaigns in the Little Havana neighborhood on Aug. 29, 2026, in Miami, Fla. (Joe Raedle/Getty Images)

"To the extent that contributions to the charity were used to pay the rent and expenses of the for-profit Café Resistance Bookstore and Coffee Shop, which in turn was used for Angie Nixon’s political campaign, that is a clear violation of 501(c)(3) rules that prohibit charities from using their funds for political campaign purposes," the document reads.

title: Poll shows Hochul adding to lead over Blakeman in New York governor's race: 'Running out of time'
summary: New York Gov. Kathy Hochul leads Bruce Blakeman by 14 points in a Siena poll, but a plurality of voters say neither will make life more affordable.
story: New York gubernatorial candidate Bruce Blakeman joins 'Sunday Morning Futures' to discuss his campaign, Kathy Hochul's record and New York taxes under her leadership.

New York Gov. Kathy Hochul expanded her lead over Republican challenger Bruce Blakeman to double digits in a new poll showing the Democratic incumbent pulling further ahead in the final days before Election Day.

Hochul leads the Nassau County executive 54% to 40% among likely New York voters, according to a Siena Research Institute survey released Wednesday. The 14-point margin is five points wider than her lead in September, when she led 50% to 41%.

"Heading into the final stretch, Hochul has a 14-point lead, with Blakeman quickly running out of time to close a gap that is growing rather than narrowing," Siena pollster Steven Greenberg said in a statement.
NEW YORK GOVERNOR DEBATE HEATS UP AS BLAKEMAN, HOCHUL SPAR OVER TRUMP, SANCTUARY STATUS, ICE SHOOTING
Nassau County Executive Bruce Blakeman, left, and New York Gov. Kathy Hochul. (NDZ/Star Max/GC Images/Getty Images; Alexander MacDougall/Albany Times Union via Getty Images)

The poll also showed Blakeman struggling to establish an advantage in areas where Republicans typically need strong support to compete statewide. The candidates are virtually tied in upstate New York and the downstate suburbs, while Hochul leads independent voters by 11 points.

Republicans generally need strong margins in those regions and among independents to overcome Democrats' roughly two-to-one voter registration advantage and their dominance in New York City, Greenberg noted.

"But with only a week to go, Blakeman and Hochul are running virtually evenly upstate and in the downstate suburbs, while Hochul has an 11-point lead with independents," Greenberg said, noting that Blakeman is "quickly running out of time to close a gap that is growing rather than narrowing."
Despite Hochul's overall advantage, the survey revealed uncertainty among voters over whether either candidate would make life more affordable for average New Yorkers.
DEBRA MESSING SAYS COST OF LIVING, SUBWAY VIOLENCE PUSHED HER TO BACK TRUMP-ENDORSED REPUBLICAN
A plurality of voters, 35%, said neither candidate would make life more affordable, compared with 30% who chose Hochul and 27% who selected Blakeman.
Kathy Hochul holds a commanding lead in New York’s race for governor. (Noam Galai/Getty Images; Mike Egerton/PA Images via Getty Images)

Hochul also reached a new milestone in the survey, with 51% of likely voters viewing her favorably compared with 45% who viewed her unfavorably. It marked the first time a majority of voters had viewed her favorably in Siena polling during her five years as governor.
Her job approval rating also rose to 51%, up from 48% in September. Blakeman, meanwhile, received a 39% favorable rating and a 40% unfavorable rating.

The survey found a sizable gender gap, with Hochul leading Blakeman by 23 points among women and six points among men. She also led among Black voters, 81% to 16%, while White voters were closely divided.

The poll also found that 68% of likely voters believed Hochul would win the election, compared with 23% who predicted a Blakeman victory. Among Republicans surveyed, 40% said they expected Hochul to win.

Gov. Kathy Hochul and Republican challenger Bruce Blakeman face off in the only scheduled debate ahead of the November New York gubernatorial election on Tuesday, Oct. 13, 2026, in New York. (Anna Connors/Pool The New York Times)

In New York's other statewide races, Democratic Attorney General Letitia James led Republican Saritha Komatireddy 54% to 39%, while Democratic state Comptroller Tom DiNapoli led Republican Joseph Hernandez 59% to 32%.
The Siena poll was conducted Oct. 19–22 among 807 likely New York voters through telephone and text-to-web surveys. It has a margin of error of plus or minus 4.1 percentage points.

title: 50,000 airline miles stolen from a travel expert
summary: Travel expert Katy Nastro says 50,000 American Airlines AAdvantage miles vanished from her account after someone redeemed them without permission.
story: Travel expert Katy Nastro tells Kurt ‘CyberGuy’ Knutsson that someone used her American Airlines miles and explained why saving your travel rewards may not pay off.

If you're anything like me, you've probably spent years collecting airline miles, dreaming about the trip you'll eventually take. Maybe it's a business class seat to Europe or that vacation you've been putting off. You keep earning points and watching the balance grow. But what happens when you finally check your account and discover someone else has already spent them?

That's exactly what happened to Katy Nastro, a travel expert with Flighty, a flight-tracking app that provides real-time updates on delays, cancellations and gate changes. During our conversation on "The CyberGuy Report" podcast, Katy shared how more than 50,000 American Airlines miles vanished from her account. Someone had redeemed them for a flight without her permission.

What surprised me was that Katy knows the travel industry inside and out. Yet she still found herself dealing with a problem that could happen to anyone with a frequent flyer account. Her experience offers a warning, especially as holiday travel approaches.
9 WARNING SIGNS OF IDENTITY THEFT YOU SHOULD NEVER IGNORE

No technical experience is needed.

Travel expert Katy Nastro discovered that someone had redeemed 50,000 American Airlines miles from her account without permission. (Mark Felix/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
How a travel expert discovered 50,000 stolen airline miles

Katy had just landed in New York and was riding home in an Uber. Like many frequent travelers, she opened her American Airlines app to check how many miles she'd earned from her latest trip. Instead, she noticed a substantial drop in her balance. At first, she figured the app had made a mistake. She remembered redeeming about 10,000 miles recently, but the balance was off by roughly 50,000. So she refreshed the app. The missing miles were still missing. That's when she called American Airlines.

The airline told her that someone had redeemed the miles for a ticket in another person's name. Katy had been saving for a trip to Asia. Unfortunately, those miles were now associated with a flight she knew nothing about.
"I really had this just stomach drop moment," Katy told me.
She had spent years earning those rewards, including through long flights to Australia. Suddenly, someone else had benefited from all that travel.
"I naively never thought this could happen to me because I work in the industry," she admitted.
I found that particularly revealing. Katy had previously warned people about loyalty account theft. Even with that experience, she never expected to become a victim herself.
Getting stolen airline miles back was surprisingly complicated

You might assume the airline could simply reverse an unauthorized redemption. After all, the ticket was booked in someone else's name. Unfortunately, Katy discovered that getting her miles back required additional work. American Airlines instructed her to submit a formal fraud complaint by email. She also had to file a police report and provide documentation before the airline would restore her miles.
"I had to have the police report filed with them before anything was credited," Katy explained.

She eventually recovered her miles, but the process didn't end there. Katy also had to create a new email address and establish a replacement American Airlines AAdvantage account. Thankfully, the airline transferred her existing status along with her restored rewards. What caught my attention was the police report requirement. Katy had to involve local law enforcement even though the theft happened entirely online. She understood why the airline might want official documentation, but she questioned whether the process needed to be so cumbersome.

There's another concern for travelers. Airline loyalty points generally don't carry the same protections as money stolen through an unauthorized credit card purchase. In fact, American Airlines' current AAdvantage terms say the airline has no general obligation to restore miles withdrawn without authorization.

The company may review requests submitted within three months of the unauthorized withdrawal, but reimbursement remains discretionary. That makes discovering suspicious activity quickly especially important. Also, keep in mind that each loyalty program has its own fraud procedures. A police report may be requested, but the requirement isn't universal.
How thieves turn stolen airline miles into real trips

I asked Katy something that had been bothering me. Who was actually flying around using her miles? She had no idea. The airline identified a redemption involving someone else's name, but Katy didn't know who was behind it or where the traveler was headed. Loyalty programs often allow members to book tickets for other people. Some also permit mileage transfers or gifts. Those legitimate features can create opportunities for criminals who gain unauthorized access to an account.

For example, someone who controls your account could redeem miles for a ticket under another person's name. Depending on the program, the points might also be transferred or exchanged for other rewards. However, Katy never learned exactly how someone accessed her account. During our conversation, she acknowledged that password reuse may have played a role.
"I think I fell into the trap of using the same password for everything," she said.

That's an easy habit to fall into. If criminals obtain a password from one compromised service, they may try using it to access other accounts. And here's something worth remembering. A loyalty balance may look like a collection of numbers on your screen, but those numbers can pay for expensive flights.
Why saving airline miles forever could cost you
Katy shared another piece of advice that might surprise anyone who's been patiently saving miles for years. She believes travelers should think twice about holding on to their rewards indefinitely.
"I would highly suggest that you should not be waiting on those miles," she told me.

Her concern comes down to depreciation. Airlines can change their award pricing, which means a flight that once required 50,000 miles might eventually require considerably more. I compared holding on to miles to buying a new car and watching its value drop after driving off the lot. Katy agreed. In her view, people often wait too long for that perfect first-class redemption. She recommends considering redemptions within a year instead of endlessly saving for a future trip.

Of course, you still want to check whether an award flight offers reasonable value. Spending 80,000 miles on an inexpensive economy ticket could be a poor deal. However, if you need to travel during a busy holiday period, using miles for an economy seat may make sense.

Award tickets can also offer more flexibility than certain restrictive cash fares. Just check the airline's cancellation and redeposit rules before booking. We've shared more strategies in our article, Are airline miles still worth it?
And if you're looking to earn more rewards for your next trip, check out my picks for the best airline credit cards of 2026 at CyberGuy.com to see which programs might work best for you.
YOUR CREDIT CAN LOOK NORMAL WHILE SOMEONE STEALS YOUR IDENTITY
Travelers spend years earning airline miles, but stolen rewards can disappear before they ever reach their dream destination. (iStock)
Watch out for fake airline alerts and customer service scams

During our conversation, I told Katy about something I've been seeing more frequently. I receive emails that look like legitimate airline notifications, claiming miles were redeemed from my account. Some are convincing enough that I've nearly clicked them myself. That's a particularly sneaky approach because many airlines send real notifications when members redeem rewards. Criminals can imitate those messages to create panic and lure people toward fake login pages.

Katy warned that scammers also create fake airline support accounts on social media. Someone looking for help with a delayed flight or missing miles might contact what appears to be an official account. The conversation can then move to a private message or even WhatsApp, where the criminal asks for personal information. Katy's warning was clear. Avoid sharing sensitive account information through social media conversations. If you receive a suspicious redemption notice, open the airline's official app yourself. Check your account activity directly rather than following links in the message.
How to protect your airline miles and hotel points

Before your next trip, take a few minutes to secure the loyalty accounts you've spent years building. These steps can help you spot unauthorized activity sooner and make your accounts harder to compromise.

Open your airline and hotel loyalty apps at least once a month. Review recent redemptions and compare your current balance with what you expected. Katy said she sometimes went several months without checking her account. That made it harder to know when the unauthorized redemption occurred. Setting a recurring calendar reminder can help you catch unusual activity sooner. Also, enable account activity and redemption alerts if your loyalty program offers them. That way, you may find out about suspicious transactions before you notice missing miles.

Never reuse your airline password on another website. A password manager can generate strong, unique passwords and store them securely. Also, protect the email account connected to your loyalty program. Someone who gains access to that inbox may be able to reset your rewards password.

Look for two-factor authentication (2FA), passkeys or other login verification options offered by your airline or hotel program. These protections vary by provider, so check your account's security settings. Also, review any unfamiliar changes to your contact information and remove devices or sessions you no longer recognize when the service allows it.

If an email or text claims someone used your points, resist clicking its links. Instead, open the official airline app or type the website address into your browser. Legitimate-looking logos and familiar formatting offer no guarantee that a message is genuine.

Also, be skeptical of anyone claiming to represent airline support through an unsolicited social media message. Use strong antivirus software to help detect malicious links, block dangerous websites and protect against malware designed to steal your passwords. While antivirus software can't stop every phishing scam, it provides an additional layer of protection if you accidentally click something suspicious.
Get my picks for the best 2026 antivirus protection winners for your Windows, Mac, Android and iOS devices at CyberGuy.com.
FAKE BOOKING.COM TRAVEL CREDIT SCAM TARGETS TRAVELERS
Regularly checking your airline miles balance and securing your loyalty accounts can help protect your hard-earned travel rewards. (iStock)

Contact your loyalty program through its verified customer service channels as soon as you notice an unauthorized redemption. Ask the airline to secure your account and investigate the transaction. Save your account statements and any correspondence. If the airline requests a police report, follow its instructions and keep a copy. Don't delay because some programs impose deadlines on fraud claims.

Katy suggested using a dedicated email address for loyalty programs. That can make account notifications easier to track and reduce exposure if an unrelated service suffers a breach. Another option is to use an email alias, which helps keep your primary address private. It lets you create unlimited email aliases, helping you organize travel accounts while reducing spam and unwanted exposure. You can also follow my guide on how to create and use email aliases.
For recommendations on private and secure email providers that offer alias addresses, visit CyberGuy.com.

Your personal information may already be circulating on data broker websites, making it easier for scammers to target you with convincing airline phishing emails or impersonation attempts. Consider using a personal data removal service. It helps remove your personal information from hundreds of data broker and people search sites and continues submitting removal requests when your details reappear. While no service can erase everything or directly prevent someone from stealing your airline miles, reducing your online exposure can make it harder for scammers to gather personal details and tailor their attacks.
Check out my top picks for data removal services and get a free scan to find out if your personal information is already out on the web by visiting CyberGuy.com.

Be careful about sharing photos of boarding passes, luggage tags or travel confirmations online. These documents can contain booking reference numbers, frequent flyer details or barcodes that expose information about your trip. Criminals may use those details to access reservations or impersonate travelers. Avoid posting travel documents on social media, and securely dispose of printed boarding passes after your trip.

You can use an AI assistant like ChatGPT with scheduled tasks to monitor airline loyalty programs for changes that could reduce the value of your miles. Set up a daily alert to check for announced changes to redemption rates, award pricing or loyalty program rules. You can even ask it to track news about American Airlines AAdvantage or other programs you use.

That way, you may hear about upcoming changes while there's still time to redeem your miles at current rates. Keep in mind that airlines don't always announce devaluations in advance, so AI can't predict every change. For step-by-step guidance, check out my article on 8 seriously annoying tasks you can hand off to an AI agent.
Kurt's key takeaways

I keep thinking about Katy sitting in the back of that Uber, casually checking her mileage balance and discovering that 50,000 hard-earned miles had disappeared. I've collected airline miles for years, and I know how much planning goes into using them. The thought of some stranger enjoying a trip on my points would make me furious. What concerns me even more is that Katy works in the travel industry and still couldn't explain exactly how someone got into her account.

That tells me we should give our loyalty accounts the same attention we give our financial accounts. Check your balances, use unique passwords and pay attention to unusual activity. And while I love saving miles for a great trip, Katy makes a convincing argument for enjoying those rewards while they still offer good value.

I encourage you to listen to The CyberGuy Report podcast at cyberguy.com/podcast/ to hear my full conversation with Katy Nastro. Her experience might change how you think about the miles you've been collecting. And if you want more ways to make those rewards go further, visit CyberGuyLive.com to sign up for my free upcoming webinar: 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money on Oct. 31 at 11 AM ET/8 AM PT.
